sentences.zh: 【晉紀十二】　起強圉赤奮若，盡著雍攝提格，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Chronicle Twelve] — from Qiangyu Chifenruo through Zhuoyong Shotige, two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Chronicle 12 — from the year Qiangyu Chifenruo through Zhuoyong Shotige, spanning two years.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝上建武元年（

translations.literal: First year of Jianwu, first part of Emperor Yuan of Zhongzong (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Jianwu under Emperor Yuan of Zhongzong (

sentences.zh: 丁丑，公元三一七年）

translations.literal: dingchou, corresponding to 317 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingchou, 317 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，漢兵東略弘農，太守宋哲奔江東。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Han forces raided east into Hongnong; the prefect Song Zhe fled to Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Han troops pushed east into Hongnong, and Prefect Song Zhe fled to the lower Yangtze region.

sentences.zh: 黃門郎史淑、侍御史王沖自長安奔涼州，稱愍帝出降前一日，使淑等繼詔賜張實，拜實大都督、涼州牧、侍中、司空，承製行事，且曰：「朕已詔琅邪王時攝大位，君其協贊琅邪，共濟多難。」

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Gentleman Shi Shu and Attending Censor Wang Chong fled from Chang'an to Liangzhou, stating that on the day before Emperor Min surrendered, he had sent Shu and the others with a follow-up edict to confer on Zhang Shi the titles of Grand Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Liangzhou, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Works, to act by imperial appointment, and saying: "I have already ordered the Prince of Langya to provisionally assume the supreme position; you should assist and support Langya to together relieve our many calamities."
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Shi Shu and Attending Censor Wang Chong fled from Chang'an to Liangzhou. They said that on the eve of Emperor Min's surrender he had dispatched them with a supplementary edict appointing Zhang Shi Grand Commander-in-Chief, Governor of Liangzhou, Palace Attendant, and Minister of Works, with authority to govern by imperial mandate. The message read: "I have already instructed the Prince of Langya to hold the supreme position for the time being. Assist him and help us through these many trials together."

sentences.zh: 淑等至姑臧，實大臨三日，辭官不受。

translations.literal: When Shu and the others reached Guzang, Zhang Shi greatly mourned for three days and declined the offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu and his party reached Guzang, Zhang Shi observed deep mourning for three days and refused the appointments.

sentences.zh: 初，實叔父肅為西海太守，聞長安危逼，請為先鋒入援。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Shi's uncle Su was Governor of Xihai; hearing that Chang'an was in peril, he asked to serve as vanguard in a relief expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Shi's uncle Su, who was governor of Xihai, heard that Chang'an was in grave danger and volunteered to lead the vanguard in relief.

sentences.zh: 實以其老，弗許。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi, considering him old, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi refused, citing his uncle's age.

sentences.zh: 及聞長安不守，肅悲憤而卒。

translations.literal: When he heard that Chang'an had fallen, Su died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Chang'an had been lost, Su died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 實遣太府司馬韓璞、撫戎將軍張閬等帥步騎一萬東擊漢，命討虜將軍陳安、安故太守賈騫、隴西太守吳紹各統郡兵為前驅。

translations.literal: Zhang Shi sent Grand Treasury Marshal Han Pu, Pacification General Zhang Lang, and others at the head of ten thousand infantry and cavalry east to attack the Han, ordering Bandit-Suppressing General Chen An, Prefect of Angu Jia Qian, and Governor of Longxi Wu Shao each to command district troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi dispatched Grand Treasury Marshal Han Pu and Pacification General Zhang Lang with ten thousand foot and horse soldiers east against the Han state, while Bandit-Suppressing General Chen An, Angu Prefect Jia Qian, and Longxi Governor Wu Shao were each to lead their district forces as the advance guard.

sentences.zh: 又遺相國保書曰：「王室有事，不忘投軀。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Chancellor Bao saying: "When the royal house is in trouble, one does not forget to offer one's life.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Chancellor Bao: "When the house of Jin is in crisis, one must not hesitate to lay down one's life.

sentences.zh: 前遣賈騫瞻公舉動，中被符命，敕騫還軍。

translations.literal: Previously I sent Jia Qian to observe your movements, but midway he received an imperial command ordering Qian to withdraw his army.
translations.idiomatic: I had earlier sent Jia Qian to watch your movements, but he was met midway by an imperial order commanding him to turn back.

sentences.zh: 俄聞寇逼長安，胡崧不進，麴允持金五百，請救於崧，遂決遣騫等進軍度嶺。

translations.literal: Soon afterward we heard that invaders were pressing Chang'an; Hu Song did not advance, and Qu Yun, bearing five hundred in gold, begged Song for aid, whereupon it was decided to send Qian and the others forward across the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the enemy was closing on Chang'an. Hu Song would not move forward, and Qu Yun took five hundred in gold to plead for help from him; only then was it decided to send Qian and the rest across the pass.

sentences.zh: 會聞朝廷傾覆，為忠不遂，憤痛之深，死有餘責。

translations.literal: Then we heard that the court had collapsed; loyalty was not fulfilled, and the pain and anger were so deep that death would still leave guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Then came word that the court had fallen. Loyalty had failed us, and the grief and shame were so bitter that even death would not expiate the fault.

sentences.zh: 今更遣璞等，唯公命是從。」

translations.literal: Now I send Pu and the others again; they will follow only your command."
translations.idiomatic: I now send Pu and the rest once more; they await only your orders."

sentences.zh: 璞等卒不能進而還，至南安，諸羌斷路，相持百餘日，糧竭矢盡。

translations.literal: In the end Pu and the others could not advance and turned back; reaching Nan'an, the various Qiang cut the road, and the two sides faced each other for more than a hundred days until grain and arrows were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Han Pu's force could not break through and withdrew. At Nan'an the Qiang tribes blocked the road; the standoff lasted more than a hundred days until food and arrows were gone.

sentences.zh: 璞殺車中牛以饗士，泣謂之曰：「汝曹念父母乎？」

translations.literal: Pu slaughtered the oxen from the wagons to feast the soldiers, and weeping said to them: "Do you think of your parents?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Pu had the draft oxen slaughtered to feed his men, and through tears he asked them: "Do you miss your parents?"

translations.literal: They said: "We do."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "We do."

sentences.zh: 「念妻子乎？」

translations.literal: "Do you think of your wives and children?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you miss your wives and children?"

translations.literal: They said: "We do."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "We do."

sentences.zh: 「欲生還乎？」

translations.literal: "Do you wish to return alive?"
translations.idiomatic: Do you want to get home alive?"

translations.literal: They said: "We do."
translations.idiomatic: They answered: "We do."

sentences.zh: 「從我令乎？」

translations.literal: "Will you follow my orders?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you obey my command?"

translations.literal: They said: "We will."
translations.idiomatic: They shouted: "Yes!"

sentences.zh: 乃鼓噪進戰。

translations.literal: Then with shouts and drums they advanced to battle.
translations.idiomatic: With a great clamor they charged into battle.

sentences.zh: 會張閬帥金城兵繼至，夾擊，大破之，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Lang arrived leading Jincheng troops; attacking from both sides, they inflicted a great defeat and took several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lang then arrived with troops from Jincheng; caught in a pincer, the enemy was routed and several thousand heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 先是，長安謠曰：「秦川中，血沒腕，唯有涼州倚柱觀。」

translations.literal: Earlier, a Chang'an ballad said: "In the Qin River lands, blood reaches the wrist; only in Liangzhou do people lean on pillars and watch."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a ballad in Chang'an ran: "In the Qin River country blood rises to the wrist; only in Liangzhou do folk lean on a pillar and look on."

sentences.zh: 及漢兵覆關中，氐、羌掠隴右，雍、秦之民，死者什八九，獨涼州安全。

translations.literal: When Han forces overran Guanzhong, the Di and Qiang plundered Longyou; of the people of Yong and Qin, eight or nine in ten died, while Liangzhou alone remained secure.
translations.idiomatic: When Han troops overran Guanzhong, Di and Qiang raiders swept Longyou; eight or nine out of ten people in Yong and Qin perished, and only Liangzhou was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 二月，漢主聰使從弟暢帥步騎三萬攻滎陽，太守李矩屯韓王故壘，相去七里，遣使招矩。

translations.literal: In the second month, Han ruler Cong sent his cousin Chang at the head of thirty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Xingyang; Prefect Li Ju encamped at the old fortress of King Han of Chu, seven li distant, and Chang sent envoys to summon Ju.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Han ruler Liu Cong sent his cousin Liu Chang with thirty thousand foot and horse soldiers against Xingyang. Prefect Li Ju held the old camp of King Han of Chu, seven li away, and Chang sent envoys to demand his surrender.

sentences.zh: 時暢兵猝至，矩未及為備，乃遣使詐降於暢。

translations.literal: Chang's troops had come suddenly, and Ju had not time to prepare; he therefore sent envoys to feign surrender to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's army had struck without warning, and Li Ju had no time to ready his defenses, so he sent envoys to pretend submission.

sentences.zh: 暢不復設備，大饗，渠帥皆醉。

translations.literal: Chang no longer took precautions, held a great feast, and the chieftains all became drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Chang let his guard down, threw a great feast, and his tribal leaders all drank themselves drunk.

sentences.zh: 矩欲夜襲之，士卒皆恇懼，矩乃遣其將郭誦禱於子產祠，使巫揚言曰：「子產有教，當遣神兵相助。」

translations.literal: Ju wished to attack by night, but the soldiers were all fearful; Ju then sent his general Guo Song to pray at the shrine of Zichan and had a shaman proclaim: "Zichan has instructed that divine troops will be sent to assist."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju planned a night assault, but his men were terrified. He sent General Guo Song to pray at the shrine of Zichan and had a shaman announce: "Zichan commands that spirit soldiers will come to our aid."

sentences.zh: 眾皆踴躍爭進。

translations.literal: The troops all leaped forward eagerly to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The men surged forward, each striving to be first.

sentences.zh: 矩選勇敢千人，使誦將之，掩擊暢營，斬首數千級，暢僅以身免。

translations.literal: Ju selected a thousand brave men, had Song lead them in a surprise attack on Chang's camp, and took several thousand heads; Chang barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju picked a thousand bold fighters and sent Guo Song to lead a surprise raid on Chang's camp. Several thousand heads were taken, and Chang barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，宋哲至建康，稱受愍帝詔，令丞相琅邪王睿統攝萬機。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, Song Zhe reached Jiankang, stating that he bore an edict from Emperor Min ordering Chancellor, the Prince of Langya Sima Rui, to take charge of all state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Song Zhe arrived at Jiankang with what he said was an edict from Emperor Min appointing Chancellor Sima Rui, Prince of Langya, to oversee all government business.

sentences.zh: 三月，琅邪王素服出次，舉哀三日。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Prince of Langya, in plain white garments, went out to his mourning lodge and observed lamentation for three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Langya went out in undyed mourning dress to a lodge and mourned for three days.

sentences.zh: 於是西陽王羕及官屬等共上尊號，王不許。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Xiyang, Yang, and the officials together submitted a petition for an exalted title; the prince refused.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Prince of Xiyang, Sima Yang, and the rest of the court jointly urged him to take the imperial title, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 羕等固請不已，王慨然流涕曰：「孤，罪人也。

translations.literal: Yang and the others pressed unceasingly; the prince sighed, wept, and said: "I, a solitary man, am a criminal.
translations.idiomatic: Yang and his party would not let the matter drop. The prince sighed, tears streaming, and said: "I am a guilty man.

sentences.zh: 諸賢見逼不已，當歸琅邪耳！」

translations.literal: If you gentlemen press me without end, I should simply return to Langya!"
translations.idiomatic: If you worthy men keep pressing me, I ought to go back to Langya!"

sentences.zh: 呼私奴，命駕將歸國。

translations.literal: He called a personal servant and ordered the carriage prepared to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a household servant and told him to ready the carriage for the journey home to Langya.

sentences.zh: 羕等乃請依魏、晉故事，稱晉王；

translations.literal: Yang and the others then asked that, following the precedents of Wei and Jin, he be styled Prince of Jin;
translations.idiomatic: Yang and the others then asked that, following Wei and Jin precedent, he accept the title Prince of Jin;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: he consented.
translations.idiomatic: and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，即晉王位，大赦，改元；

translations.literal: On xinmao day he assumed the title Prince of Jin, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day he took the throne as Prince of Jin, declared a general amnesty, and adopted a new era name;

sentences.zh: 始備百官，立宗廟，建社稷。

translations.literal: he began to install the full complement of officials, established the ancestral temple, and founded the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: installed the full bureaucracy, erected the ancestral temple, and established the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 有司請立太子，王愛次子宣城公裒，欲立之，謂王導曰：「立子當以德。」

translations.literal: The responsible offices asked that a crown prince be appointed; the prince favored his second son, Duke of Xuancheng, Pou, and wished to install him, saying to Wang Dao: "In choosing a son, virtue should decide."
translations.idiomatic: The officials asked that a crown prince be named. The prince favored his second son, Duke Pou of Xuancheng, and wanted to name him heir. He told Wang Dao: "A son should be chosen for his virtue."

sentences.zh: 導曰：「世子、宣城，俱有朗俊之美，而世子年長。」

translations.literal: Dao said: "The heir apparent and the Duke of Xuancheng both have bright and handsome qualities, but the heir apparent is older."
translations.idiomatic: Dao replied: "The heir apparent and the Duke of Xuancheng are both gifted and handsome, but the heir apparent is the elder."

sentences.zh: 王從之。

translations.literal: The prince followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The prince accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，立世子紹為王太子；

translations.literal: On bingchen day he installed the heir apparent Shao as crown prince;
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day he named the heir apparent Sima Shao crown prince;

sentences.zh: 封裒為琅邪王，奉恭王后；

translations.literal: he enfeoffed Pou as Prince of Langya to attend to the late Empress Gong;
translations.idiomatic: enfeoffed Pou as Prince of Langya to serve the spirit of the late Empress Gong;

sentences.zh: 仍以裒都督青、徐、兗三州諸軍事，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: and further made Pou Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan provinces, stationed at Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed him commander of all military affairs in Qing, Xu, and Yan, with his seat at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 以西陽王羕為太保，封譙剛王遜之子承為譙王。

translations.literal: He made the Prince of Xiyang, Yang, Grand Tutor, and enfeoffed Cheng, son of the Prince of Qiaogang, Sun, as Prince of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He named the Prince of Xiyang Grand Tutor and enfeoffed Cheng, son of the late Prince of Qiaogang Sima Sun, as Prince of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 遜，宣帝之弟子也。

translations.literal: Sun was a younger cousin of Emperor Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Sun had been a younger cousin of Emperor Xuan.

sentences.zh: 又以征南大將軍王敦為大將軍、江州牧，揚州刺史王導為驃騎將軍、都督中外諸軍事、領中書監、錄尚書事，丞相左長史刁協為尚書左僕射，右長史周顗為吏部尚書，軍諮祭酒賀循為中書令，右司馬戴淵、王邃為尚書，司直劉隗為御史中丞，行參軍劉超為中書舍人，參軍事孔愉長兼中書郎；

translations.literal: He also appointed Campaigning-South General Wang Dun Grand General and Governor of Jiangzhou; Governor of Yangzhou Wang Dao General of Agile Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs at home and abroad, Director of the Secretariat, and Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing; the Chancellor's Left Chief Clerk Diao Xie Vice Director of the Masters of Writing (Left); the Right Chief Clerk Zhou Yi Minister of the Civil Office; Military Adviser He Xun Director of the Secretariat; the Right Marshals Dai Yuan and Wang Sui Masters of Writing; Rectifier Liu Wei Censor-in-Chief; Acting Staff Officer Liu Chao Secretariat Attendant; and Staff Officer Kong Yu concurrently Secretariat Gentleman;
translations.idiomatic: He also named Campaigning-South General Wang Dun Grand General and governor of Jiangzhou; Yangzhou governor Wang Dao General of Agile Cavalry, supreme commander of all forces, Director of the Secretariat, and overseer of the Masters of Writing; Chancellor's left chief clerk Diao Xie vice director of the left Masters of Writing; right chief clerk Zhou Yi minister of the civil office; military adviser He Xun director of the Secretariat; right marshals Dai Yuan and Wang Sui masters of writing; rectifier Liu Wei censor-in-chief; acting staff officer Liu Chao secretariat attendant; and staff officer Kong Yu concurrent secretariat gentleman;

sentences.zh: 自餘參軍悉拜奉車都尉，掾屬拜駙馬都尉，行參軍舍人拜騎都尉。

translations.literal: all remaining staff officers were appointed Commandants of the Carriage; clerks were appointed Commandants of the Stables; and acting staff officers and attendants were appointed Commandants of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: the remaining staff officers were made commandants of the carriage corps, clerks commandants of the stable corps, and acting staff officers and attendants commandants of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 王敦辭州牧，王導以敦統六州，辭中外都督，賀循以老病辭中書令，王皆許之，以循為太常。

translations.literal: Wang Dun declined the governorship; Wang Dao, because Dun commanded six provinces, declined the post of commander at home and abroad; He Xun, citing age and illness, declined the directorate of the Secretariat; the prince granted all these requests and made He Xun Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun declined the governorship; Wang Dao, noting that Dun already controlled six provinces, declined supreme military command; He Xun pleaded age and illness to step down as director of the Secretariat; the prince granted each request and named He Xun Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 是時，承喪亂之後，江東草創，刁協久宦中朝，諳練舊事，賀循為世儒宗，明習禮學，凡有疑議，皆取決焉。

translations.literal: At this time, in the aftermath of the great disorders, the lower Yangtze was being built up from nothing; Diao Xie had long served in the central court and was versed in old precedents; He Xun was the leading Confucian scholar of the age and thoroughly understood ritual learning; whenever there was a doubtful point, judgment was sought from them.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was still recovering from civil collapse, and the southeast was being organized from scratch. Diao Xie had served for years at the central court and knew its precedents inside out; He Xun was the age's foremost ritual scholar. On any disputed point, the court turned to them.

sentences.zh: 劉琨、段匹磾相與歃血同盟，期以翼戴晉室。

translations.literal: Liu Kun and Duan Pidi swore a blood alliance with each other, pledging to support and uphold the house of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Duan Pidi sealed a blood oath, pledging together to uphold the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，琨檄告華、夷，遣兼左長史、右司馬溫嶠，匹磾遣左長史榮邵，奉表及盟文詣建康勸進。

translations.literal: On xinchou day Liu Kun issued a proclamation to Chinese and barbarians alike, sending his concurrent Left Chief Clerk and Right Marshal Wen Jiao; Duan Pidi sent his Left Chief Clerk Rong Shao to present memorials and the text of the alliance to Jiankang urging the prince to advance.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Liu Kun issued a proclamation to all under heaven and sent his concurrent left chief clerk and right marshal Wen Jiao to Jiankang; Duan Pidi sent his left chief clerk Rong Shao with memorials and the alliance text urging the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 嶠，羨之弟子也。

translations.literal: Jiao was a nephew of Wen Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Jiao was a nephew of the Jin minister Wen Xian.

sentences.zh: 嶠之從母為琨妻，琨謂嶠曰：「晉祚雖衰，天命未改，吾當立功河朔，使卿延譽江南。

translations.literal: Jiao's father's sister was Liu Kun's wife; Kun said to Jiao: "Though the fortune of Jin has declined, the Mandate has not shifted; I shall establish merit on the north bank of the Yellow River and enable you to win renown in the south.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao's aunt was Liu Kun's wife. Kun told him: "Jin's fortunes may be low, but Heaven's mandate has not changed. I will win glory north of the Yellow River, and you will carry our name into the south.

sentences.zh: 行矣，勉之！」

translations.literal: Go now, and strive hard!"
translations.idiomatic: Go, and do your utmost!"

sentences.zh: 王以鮮卑大都督慕容廆為都督遼左雜夷流民諸軍事、龍驤將軍、大單于、昌黎公，廆不受；

translations.literal: The prince appointed the Xianbei Grand Commander Murong Hui Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs concerning mixed tribes and displaced people in eastern Liaodong, General of Dragon Cavalry, Grand Chanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui did not accept;
translations.idiomatic: The prince appointed the Xianbei leader Murong Hui commander of military affairs for eastern Liaodong tribes and refugees, General of Dragon Cavalry, Grand Chanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui declined;

sentences.zh: 征虜將軍魯昌說廆曰：「今兩京覆沒，天子蒙塵，琅邪王承製江東，為四海所繫屬。

translations.literal: Campaigning-Barbarian General Lu Chang urged Hui, saying: "Now the two capitals have fallen, the Son of Heaven suffers in exile, and the Prince of Langya holds power by imperial appointment in the lower Yangtze; all within the four seas look to him.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning-Barbarian General Lu Chang urged Murong Hui: "Both capitals are lost, the emperor is in exile, and the Prince of Langya governs the southeast by imperial mandate. The whole realm is looking to him.

sentences.zh: 明公雖雄據一方，而諸部猶阻兵未服者，蓋以官非王命故也。

translations.literal: Though you, my lord, hold a region with heroic strength, some tribes still keep their arms and will not submit, largely because your office is not conferred by the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: You hold your territory by force, yet some tribes still resist, largely because your rank did not come from the court.

sentences.zh: 謂宜通使琅邪，勸承大統，然後奉詔令以伐有罪，誰敢不從！」

translations.literal: I hold that you should send envoys to Langya, urge him to assume the great succession, and then, bearing imperial orders, punish the guilty — who would dare not obey!"
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to Langya, urge him to take the throne, and then campaign under imperial orders against wrongdoers — who would refuse to follow?"

sentences.zh: 處士遼東高詡曰：「霸王之資，非義不濟。

translations.literal: The recluse Gao Xu of Liaodong said: "The resources of a hegemon king cannot succeed without righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The hermit Gao Xu of Liaodong said: "He who would be a hegemon cannot succeed without righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今晉室雖微，人心猶附之，宜遣使江東，示有所尊，然後仗大義以征諸部，不患無辭矣。」

translations.literal: Though the house of Jin is now weak, men's hearts still cling to it; you should send envoys to the lower Yangtze to show whom you honor, and then, relying on great righteousness, campaign against the tribes — you need not fear lacking justification."
translations.idiomatic: Jin may be weak, but loyalty to it still runs deep. Send envoys east to show whom you acknowledge, then march on the tribes under the banner of righteousness, and you will never lack a just cause."

sentences.zh: 廆從之，遣長史王濟浮海詣建康勸進。

translations.literal: Hui followed this advice and sent Chief Clerk Wang Ji by sea to Jiankang to urge advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Hui took their counsel and sent his chief clerk Wang Ji across the sea to Jiankang to urge the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 漢相國粲使其黨王平謂太弟義曰：「適奉中詔，雲京師將有變，宜衷甲以備非常。」

translations.literal: Han Chancellor of State Can had his partisan Wang Ping tell the Grand Heir Apparent Yi: "I have just received an inner edict saying that the capital will soon see unrest; you should wear armor under your robes to guard against the unexpected."
translations.idiomatic: Han chancellor Liu Can sent his follower Wang Ping to the Grand Heir Apparent Liu Yi with a message: "I have just received a secret edict warning of trouble in the capital. Wear armor beneath your robes against any emergency."

sentences.zh: 義信之，命宮臣皆衷甲以居。

translations.literal: Yi believed him and ordered all palace officials to wear armor under their garments at home.
translations.idiomatic: Yi believed him and ordered every official in the Eastern Palace to wear hidden armor at all times.

sentences.zh: 粲馳遣告靳准、王沈。

translations.literal: Can hurriedly sent word to Jin Zhun and Wang Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Can at once sent word to Jin Zhun and Wang Shen.

sentences.zh: 准以白漢主聰曰：「太弟將為亂，已衷甲矣！」

translations.literal: Zhun reported to Han ruler Cong: "The Grand Heir Apparent is about to rebel — he is already wearing armor under his robes!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhun told Han ruler Liu Cong: "The Grand Heir Apparent is plotting rebellion — his men are already wearing armor under their robes!"

sentences.zh: 聰大驚曰：「寧有是邪！」

translations.literal: Cong was greatly alarmed and said: "Can this really be!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong was stunned. "Can that be true?"

sentences.zh: 王沈等皆曰：「臣等聞之久矣，屢言之，而陛下不之信也。」

translations.literal: Wang Shen and the others all said: "We have heard of this for a long time and reported it repeatedly, but Your Majesty would not believe us."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen and the others said: "We have known of this for a long time and told Your Majesty again and again, but you would not believe us."

sentences.zh: 聰使粲以兵圍東宮。

translations.literal: Cong ordered Can to surround the Eastern Palace with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cong ordered Can to surround the Eastern Palace with troops.

sentences.zh: 粲使准、沈收氐、羌酋長十餘人，窮問之，皆懸首高格，燒鐵灼目，酋長自誣與義謀反。

translations.literal: Can had Zhun and Shen seize more than ten Di and Qiang chieftains and interrogate them exhaustively; all were hung by the head on high frames, and iron was heated to burn their eyes, until the chieftains themselves falsely confessed to plotting rebellion with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Can had Zhun and Shen seize more than a dozen Di and Qiang chieftains and torture them. Their heads were hung high, red-hot iron was pressed to their eyes, and under torture they confessed to plotting with Yi.

sentences.zh: 聰謂沈等曰：「吾今而後知卿等之忠也！

translations.literal: Cong said to Shen and the others: "Only now do I know your loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Cong told Shen and the rest: "Only now do I see how loyal you are!

sentences.zh: 當念知無不言，勿恨往日言而不用也！」

translations.literal: Remember to speak of whatever you know without reserve, and do not resent that in the past I did not heed your words!"
translations.idiomatic: Speak out whenever you know something, and do not hold it against me that I ignored you before!"

sentences.zh: 於是誅東宮官屬及義素所親厚，准、沈等素所憎怨者大臣數十人，坑士卒萬五千餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon he executed the officials of the Eastern Palace and those whom Yi had long favored, several dozen great ministers whom Zhun, Shen, and the others had long hated, and buried alive more than fifteen thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He then executed the Eastern Palace staff and Yi's close associates, several dozen senior ministers whom Zhun and Shen had long hated, and buried alive more than fifteen thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，廢義為北海王，粲尋使准賊殺之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Yi was deposed as Prince of Beihai, and soon afterward Can had Zhun assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Yi was demoted to Prince of Beihai, and Can soon had Zhun murder him.

sentences.zh: 義形神秀爽，寬仁有器度，故士心多附之。

translations.literal: Yi was handsome in bearing and bright in spirit, generous and magnanimous, and therefore the hearts of the gentry largely attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was handsome, open-handed, and magnanimous, and the gentry's loyalty had largely rested with him.

sentences.zh: 聰聞其死，哭之慟，曰：「吾兄弟止餘二人而不相容，安得使天下知吾心邪！」

translations.literal: When Cong heard of his death, he wept bitterly and said: "Of us brothers only two remained, and we could not tolerate each other — how can I make the empire know my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: When Cong heard of his death he wailed and said: "Only two brothers were left to us, and we could not live in peace — how can I make the world understand what is in my heart?"

sentences.zh: 氐、羌叛者甚眾，以靳准行車騎大將軍，討平之。

translations.literal: Di and Qiang rebels were very numerous; Jin Zhun was appointed Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Di and Qiang rebels rose in great numbers; Jin Zhun was made acting General of Chariots and Cavalry and sent to put them down.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on renwu day, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu day, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 六月，丙寅，溫嶠等至建康，王導、周顗、庾亮等皆愛嶠才，爭與之交。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on bingyin day, Wen Jiao and the others reached Jiankang; Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Yu Liang, and the rest all admired Jiao's talent and vied to befriend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on bingyin day, Wen Jiao arrived at Jiankang. Wang Dao, Zhou Yi, Yu Liang, and others admired his gifts and competed to win his friendship.

sentences.zh: 是時，太尉、豫州牧荀組、冀州刺史邵續、青州刺史曹嶷、寧州刺史王遜、東夷校尉崔毖等皆上表勸進，王不許。

translations.literal: At this time the Grand Commandant and Governor of Yuzhou, Xun Zu; the Inspector of Jizhou, Shao Xu; the Inspector of Qingzhou, Cao Yi; the Inspector of Ningzhou, Wang Xun; and the Colonel of the Eastern Yi, Cui Bi, all submitted memorials urging advancement, but the prince would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant and Yuzhou governor Xun Zu, Jizhou inspector Shao Xu, Qingzhou inspector Cao Yi, Ningzhou inspector Wang Xun, and Colonel of the Eastern Yi Cui Bi all memorialized urging him to take the throne, but the prince again refused.

sentences.zh: 初，流民張平、樊雅各聚眾數千人在譙，為塢主。

translations.literal: Earlier, the displaced men Zhang Ping and Fan Ya had each gathered several thousand followers at Qiao and served as fortress lords.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the refugee leaders Zhang Ping and Fan Ya had each raised several thousand men at Qiao and ruled fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 王之為丞相也，遣行參軍譙國桓宣往說平、雅，平、雅皆請降。

translations.literal: When the prince was still Chancellor, he sent Acting Staff Officer Huan Xuan of Qiao to persuade Ping and Ya, and both asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: While the prince was still chancellor he sent acting staff officer Huan Xuan of Qiao to win them over, and both offered to submit.

sentences.zh: 及豫州刺史祖逖出屯蘆洲，遣參軍殷義詣平、雅。

translations.literal: When Governor of Yuzhou Zu Ti moved out to encamp at Luzhou, he sent Staff Officer Yin Yi to visit Ping and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuzhou governor Zu Ti encamped at Luzhou, he sent staff officer Yin Yi to visit Ping and Ya.

sentences.zh: 義意輕平，視其屋，曰：「可作馬廄。」

translations.literal: Yi looked down on Ping; surveying his dwelling, he said: "This could serve as a stable."
translations.idiomatic: Yi treated Ping with contempt. Looking over his house he said: "This would make a fine stable."

sentences.zh: 見大鑊，曰：「可鑄鐵器。」

translations.literal: Seeing a great cauldron, he said: "This could be cast into iron tools."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing a great cauldron, he said: "That could be melted down for ironware."

sentences.zh: 平曰：「此乃帝王鑊，天下清平方用之，奈何毀之！」

translations.literal: Ping said: "This is an imperial cauldron, to be used only when the realm is at peace — how can you speak of destroying it!"
translations.idiomatic: Ping said: "That is an imperial cauldron, meant for use only when the realm is at peace. How dare you speak of destroying it!"

sentences.zh: 義曰：「卿未能保其頭，而愛鑊邪！」

translations.literal: Yi said: "You cannot even keep your own head — yet you cherish a cauldron!"
translations.idiomatic: Yi sneered: "You cannot even keep your own head, and you care about a cauldron?"

sentences.zh: 平大怒，於坐斬義，勒兵固守。

translations.literal: Ping was furious, beheaded Yi on the spot, and marshaled his troops to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Ping flew into a rage, had Yi executed where he sat, and mobilized his men to defend the camp.

sentences.zh: 逖攻之，歲餘不下，乃誘其部將謝浮，使殺之；

translations.literal: Zu Ti attacked him, but for more than a year could not take him; he then enticed Ping's officer Xie Fu to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti besieged him for more than a year without success, then won over his officer Xie Fu and had him assassinate Ping;

sentences.zh: 逖進據太丘。

translations.literal: Zu Ti advanced and occupied Taiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti then advanced and took Taiqiu.

sentences.zh: 樊雅猶據譙城，與逖相拒。

translations.literal: Fan Ya still held Qiao city and resisted Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ya still held Qiao city and resisted Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 逖攻之不克，請兵於南中郎將王含。

translations.literal: Zu Ti attacked but could not overcome him and asked troops from the Southern Gentlemen-Commander Wang Han.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti failed to take the city and asked Southern Gentlemen-Commander Wang Han for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 桓宣時為含參軍，含遣宣將兵五百助逖。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was then on Han's staff; Han sent Xuan with five hundred men to assist Zu Ti.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was then on Han's staff; Han sent him with five hundred men to aid Zu Ti.

sentences.zh: 逖謂宣曰：「卿信義已著於彼，今復為我說雅。」

translations.literal: Zu Ti said to Xuan: "Your faith and integrity are already known to them; now go once more and persuade Ya for me."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti told Xuan: "Your good faith is already known to them. Go again and win Ya over for me."

sentences.zh: 宣乃單馬從兩人詣雅曰：「祖豫州方欲平蕩劉、石，倚卿為援；

translations.literal: Xuan then went alone on horseback with only two attendants to Ya and said: "Governor Zu of Yuzhou is about to sweep away Liu and Shi and relies on you as his support;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan rode out alone with two men and told Ya: "Governor Zu of Yuzhou is preparing to crush Liu and Shi and counts on your support;

sentences.zh: 前殷義輕薄，非豫州意也。」

translations.literal: the earlier rudeness of Yin Yi did not represent the governor's intent."
translations.idiomatic: Yin Yi's earlier insults did not reflect the governor's wishes."

sentences.zh: 雅即詣逖降。

translations.literal: Ya at once went to Zu Ti and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Ya went at once to Zu Ti and submitted.

sentences.zh: 逖既入譙城，石勒遣石虎圍譙，王含復遣桓宣救之，虎解去。

translations.literal: After Zu Ti entered Qiao city, Shi Le sent Shi Hu to besiege Qiao; Wang Han again sent Huan Xuan to the rescue, and Hu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zu Ti held Qiao, Shi Le sent Shi Hu to besiege it; Wang Han sent Huan Xuan again to relieve the city, and Hu withdrew.

sentences.zh: 逖表宣為譙國內史。

translations.literal: Zu Ti memorialized that Xuan be appointed Interior Minister of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti recommended Xuan for appointment as interior minister of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 己巳，晉王傳檄天下，稱：「石虎敢帥犬羊，渡河縱毒，今遣琅邪王裒等九軍，銳卒三萬，水陸四道，逕造賊場，受祖逖節度。」

translations.literal: On jisi day the Prince of Jin issued a proclamation to the empire, saying: "Shi Hu dares to lead dogs and sheep across the river to spread poison; I now send the Prince of Langya, Pou, and eight other armies — thirty thousand elite troops by four routes, land and water — straight to the rebel camp, under the command of Zu Ti."
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day the Prince of Jin proclaimed to the realm: "Shi Hu dares lead his barbarian hordes across the river to ravage the land. I am sending Prince Pou of Langya and eight other armies — thirty thousand picked troops by four routes, by land and water — straight against the enemy, under Zu Ti's command."

sentences.zh: 尋復召裒還建康。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he recalled Pou to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recalled Pou to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，大旱；

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, there was great drought;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, a severe drought struck;

sentences.zh: 司、冀、並、青、雍州大蝗；

translations.literal: in Sizhou, Jizhou, Bingzhou, Qingzhou, and Yongzhou locusts swarmed;
translations.idiomatic: locusts ravaged Sizhou, Jizhou, Bingzhou, Qingzhou, and Yongzhou;

sentences.zh: 河、汾溢，漂千餘家。

translations.literal: the Yellow and Fen rivers overflowed and swept away more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: and the Yellow and Fen rivers flooded, carrying off more than a thousand homes.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰立晉王粲為皇太子，領相國、大單于，總攝朝政如故。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong installed Prince of Jin, Can, as crown prince, with him holding the posts of Chancellor of State and Grand Chanyu and directing court affairs as before.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong named Prince of Jin Liu Can crown prince, retaining the posts of chancellor of state and grand chanyu and continuing to direct the government as before.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾推劉琨為大都督，檄其兄遼西公疾陸眷及叔父涉復辰、弟末柸等會於固安，共討石勒。

translations.literal: Duan Pidi urged that Liu Kun be made Grand Commander-in-Chief and issued a proclamation to his elder brother, the Duke of Liaoxi, Jilujuan, his uncle Shefuchen, his younger brother Mobei, and others to assemble at Gu'an to campaign jointly against Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi had Liu Kun named grand commander-in-chief and called on his elder brother Jilujuan, Duke of Liaoxi, his uncle Shefuchen, his younger brother Mobei, and others to meet at Gu'an for a joint campaign against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 末柸說疾陸眷、涉復辰曰：「以父兄而從子弟，恥也；

translations.literal: Mobei urged Jilujuan and Shefuchen, saying: "For elders to follow the young is shameful;
translations.idiomatic: Mobei persuaded Jilujuan and Shefuchen: "It is shameful for elders to take orders from a younger kinsman;

sentences.zh: 且幸而有功，匹磾獨收之，吾屬何有哉！」

translations.literal: and if by chance there is success, Pidi alone will reap it — what will there be for us!"
translations.idiomatic: and if we succeed, Pidi alone will claim the glory — what will be left for us?"

sentences.zh: 各引兵還。

translations.literal: Each led his troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Each withdrew with his forces.

sentences.zh: 琨、匹磾不能獨留，亦還薊。

translations.literal: Kun and Pidi could not remain alone and also returned to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to stay on alone, Kun and Pidi returned to Ji as well.

sentences.zh: 以荀組為司徒。

translations.literal: Xun Zu was appointed Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Zu was appointed Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 八月，漢趙固襲衛將軍華薈於臨穎，殺之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Zhao Gu of Han attacked Defender-in-Chief Hua Hui at Linying and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zhao Gu of the Han state attacked Defender-in-Chief Hua Hui at Linying and killed him.

sentences.zh: 初，趙固與長史周振有隙，振密譖固於漢主聰。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhao Gu and his chief clerk Zhou Zhen had been at odds; Zhen secretly slandered Gu to Han ruler Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu and his chief clerk Zhou Zhen had long been at odds, and Zhen secretly denounced Gu to Liu Cong.

sentences.zh: 李矩之破劉暢也，於帳中得聰詔，令暢既克矩，還過洛陽，收固斬之，以振代固。

translations.literal: When Li Ju defeated Liu Chang, he found in the camp an edict from Cong ordering that after Chang had overcome Ju and returned by way of Luoyang, Gu was to be seized and executed and Zhen was to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ju defeated Liu Chang he found in the enemy camp an edict from Cong instructing Chang, once Ju was beaten, to arrest and execute Gu on the way back through Luoyang and install Zhen in his place.

sentences.zh: 矩送以示固，固斬振父子，帥騎一千來降；

translations.literal: Ju sent it to show Gu; Gu executed Zhen and his son, led a thousand horsemen to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Ju showed the edict to Gu, who executed Zhen and his son and came over with a thousand horsemen;

sentences.zh: 矩復令固守洛陽。

translations.literal: Ju again ordered Gu to hold Luoyang firmly.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Ju again put him in charge of defending Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭攀等相與拒王廙，眾心不壹，散還橫桑口，欲入杜曾。

translations.literal: Zheng Pan and others jointly resisted Wang Yi, but hearts were not united; they dispersed back to Hengsangkou, intending to join Du Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Pan and others resisted Wang Yi together, but their forces were divided; they fell back to Hengsangkou planning to join Du Zeng.

sentences.zh: 王敦遣武昌太守趙誘、襄陽太守朱軌擊之，攀等懼，請降。

translations.literal: Wang Dun sent the Prefect of Wuchang, Zhao You, and the Prefect of Xiangyang, Zhu Gui, to attack them; Pan and the others were afraid and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun sent Wuchang prefect Zhao You and Xiangyang prefect Zhu Gui against them; Pan and his men were frightened and offered to submit.

sentences.zh: 杜曾亦請擊第五猗於襄陽以自贖。

translations.literal: Du Zeng also asked to attack the Fifth Yi at Xiangyang to redeem himself.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng also offered to attack the Fifth Yi at Xiangyang to atone for his crimes.

sentences.zh: 廙將赴荊州，留長史劉浚鎮揚口壘。

translations.literal: Yi was about to go to Jingzhou and left Chief Clerk Liu Jun to guard the fortress at Yangkou.
translations.idiomatic: As Wang Yi prepared to take up his post in Jingzhou, he left chief clerk Liu Jun to hold the fort at Yangkou.

sentences.zh: 竟陵內史朱伺謂廙曰：「曾，猾賊也，外示屈服，欲誘官軍使西，然後兼道襲揚口耳。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Jingling Zhu Si said to Yi: "Zeng is a cunning bandit who outwardly shows submission, intending to lure the government army west and then strike Yangkou by another route.
translations.idiomatic: Jingling interior minister Zhu Si warned Yi: "Du Zeng is a cunning rebel. His surrender is a ruse to draw our army west, then strike Yangkou from another direction.

sentences.zh: 宜大部分，未可便西。」

translations.literal: You should keep the main force here and not move west at once."
translations.idiomatic: Keep the bulk of your force here; do not march west yet."

sentences.zh: 廙性矜厲自用，以伺為老怯，遂西行。

translations.literal: Yi was proud and self-willed by nature; he took Si for an old coward and marched west.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was proud and headstrong; he dismissed Si as timid in his old age and marched west.

sentences.zh: 曾等果還趨揚口；

translations.literal: Zeng and the others did indeed turn back and hurry to Yangkou;
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng did turn back toward Yangkou;

sentences.zh: 廙乃遣伺歸，裁至壘，即為曾所圍。

translations.literal: Yi then sent Si back, but as soon as he reached the fortress he was surrounded by Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi sent Si back, but the moment he reached the fort Du Zeng had it surrounded.

sentences.zh: 劉浚自守北門，使伺守南門。

translations.literal: Liu Jun himself held the north gate and had Si hold the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun held the north gate himself and put Si in charge of the south gate.

sentences.zh: 馬俊從曾來攻壘，俊妻子先在壘中，或欲皮其面以示之。

translations.literal: Ma Jun came with Zeng to attack the fortress; Jun's wife and children were already inside, and some wished to flay their faces to show him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Jun came with Du Zeng to assault the fort. Jun's wife and children were inside, and some proposed flaying their faces and displaying them to him.

sentences.zh: 伺曰：「殺其妻子，未能解圍，但益其怒耳。」

translations.literal: Si said: "Killing his wife and children will not lift the siege; it will only increase his rage."
translations.idiomatic: Si said: "Killing his family will not break the siege; it will only make him fight harder."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: They stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They desisted.

sentences.zh: 曾攻陷北門，伺被傷，退入船，開船底以出，沉行五十步，乃得免。

translations.literal: Zeng stormed the north gate; Si was wounded, retreated into a boat, opened the bottom to escape, and swam submerged for fifty paces before he got free.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng broke through the north gate. Wounded, Si retreated into a boat, escaped through a hole cut in the hull, and swam underwater fifty paces before he got away.

sentences.zh: 曾遣人說伺曰：「馬俊德卿全其妻子，今盡以卿家內外百口付俊，俊已盡心收視，卿可來也。」

translations.literal: Zeng sent someone to tell Si: "Ma Jun, out of regard for you, spared your wife and children; I have now entrusted all your kin, inside and outside, more than a hundred persons, to Jun, and he is caring for them with full diligence — you may come."
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng sent word: "Out of respect for you, Ma Jun spared your family. I have placed all your kin, more than a hundred people, in his care. Come back."

sentences.zh: 伺報曰：「吾年六十餘，不能復與卿作賊，吾死亦當南歸，妻子付汝裁之。」

translations.literal: Si replied: "I am more than sixty and cannot again be a bandit with you; even in death I shall return south — do as you will with my wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: Si replied: "I am past sixty and will not be your accomplice again. Even dead I belong in the south — my family is in your hands."

sentences.zh: 乃就王廙於甑山，病創而卒。

translations.literal: He then went to Wang Yi at Zengshan and died of his wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Wang Yi at Zengshan and died of his wounds.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，趙誘、朱軌及陵江將軍黃峻與曾戰於女觀湖，誘等皆敗死。

translations.literal: On wuyin day Zhao You, Zhu Gui, and General Who Crosses the River Huang Jun fought Zeng at Nüguan Lake; You and the others were all defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Zhao You, Zhu Gui, and General Who Crosses the River Huang Jun met Du Zeng at Nüguan Lake and were defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 曾乘勝徑告沔口，威震江、沔。

translations.literal: Zeng pressed his victory straight to Hankou, and his prestige shook the Yangtze and Han regions.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng pressed his victory straight to Hankou, and his power terrified the Yangtze and Han valleys.

sentences.zh: 王使豫章太守周訪擊之。

translations.literal: The prince sent the Prefect of Yuzhang, Zhou Fang, to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The prince sent Yuzhang prefect Zhou Fang against him.

sentences.zh: 訪有眾八千，進至沌陽。

translations.literal: Fang had eight thousand men and advanced to Zhunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had eight thousand men and advanced to Zhunyang.

sentences.zh: 曾銳氣甚盛，訪使將軍李恆督左甄，許朝督右甄，訪自領中軍。

translations.literal: Zeng's fighting spirit was very high; Fang had General Li Heng command the left wing, Xu Chao the right wing, and took the center himself.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng's troops were fierce. Fang put General Li Heng in charge of the left wing, Xu Chao the right, and kept the center under his own command.

sentences.zh: 曾先攻左、右甄，訪於陣後射雉以安眾心，令其眾曰：「一甄敗，鳴三鼓；

translations.literal: Zeng first attacked the left and right wings; Fang shot pheasants behind the lines to steady his men's hearts and told the army: "If one wing is beaten, beat the drum three times;
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng attacked both wings first. Fang shot pheasants behind the lines to steady his men and told them: "If one wing falls, sound three drumbeats;

sentences.zh: 兩甄敗，鳴六鼓。」

translations.literal: if both wings are beaten, beat six times."
translations.idiomatic: if both wings fall, sound six."

sentences.zh: 趙誘子胤，將父餘兵屬左甄，力戰，敗而復合，馳馬告訪。

translations.literal: Zhao You's son Yin, leading his father's remaining troops on the left wing, fought fiercely, was beaten and re-formed, and galloped to report to Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao You's son Yin led his father's survivors on the left wing, fought desperately, re-formed after a rout, and galloped to report to Fang.

sentences.zh: 訪怒，叱令更進，胤號哭還戰。

translations.literal: Fang was angry, shouted at him to advance again, and Yin, weeping aloud, returned to battle.
translations.idiomatic: Fang roared at him to attack again, and Yin, sobbing, rode back into the fight.

sentences.zh: 自旦至申，兩甄皆敗。

translations.literal: From dawn to the shen hour both wings were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: From dawn until mid-afternoon both wings were broken.

sentences.zh: 訪選精銳八百人，自行酒飲之，敕不得妄動，聞鼓音乃進。

translations.literal: Fang chose eight hundred elite troops, personally gave them wine to drink, and ordered that they must not move rashly but advance only on hearing the drum.
translations.idiomatic: Fang picked eight hundred elite troops, poured them wine himself, and forbade them to stir until they heard his drum.

sentences.zh: 曾兵未至三十步，訪親鳴鼓，將士皆騰躍奔赴，曾遂大潰，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: When Zeng's troops were still thirty paces away, Fang himself beat the drum; officers and men all leaped forward, Zeng was utterly routed, and more than a thousand were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy was still thirty paces off, Fang beat the drum himself. His men surged forward, Du Zeng's army collapsed, and more than a thousand were killed.

sentences.zh: 訪夜追之，諸將請待明日，訪曰：「曾驍勇能戰，向者彼勞我逸，故克之；

translations.literal: Fang pursued by night; the generals asked to wait until the next day, but Fang said: "Zeng is fierce and able in battle; just now they were weary and we were fresh, and so we overcame them;
translations.idiomatic: Fang pursued through the night. His generals urged waiting until morning, but he said: "Du Zeng is a fierce fighter. We won because they were tired and we were fresh;

sentences.zh: 宜及其衰乘之，可滅也。」

translations.literal: we should strike while they are still weakened and can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: we must strike while they are still spent and finish them off."

sentences.zh: 乃鼓行而進，遂定漢、沔。

translations.literal: He advanced with drums beating and thereby pacified the Han and Mian regions.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on with drums beating and secured the Han and Mian valleys.

sentences.zh: 曾走保武當。

translations.literal: Zeng fled and took refuge in Wudang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Zeng fled to Wudang.

sentences.zh: 王廙始得至荊州。

translations.literal: Wang Yi was only now able to reach Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi at last reached Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 訪以功遷梁州刺史，屯襄陽。

translations.literal: For his merit Fang was transferred to Inspector of Liangzhou and encamped at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: For his victory Fang was promoted to inspector of Liangzhou and stationed at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，琅邪王裒薨。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei day, the Prince of Langya, Pou, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, on dingwei day Prince Pou of Langya died.

sentences.zh: 十一月，己酉朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiyou, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of jiyou day, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以劉琨為待中、太尉。

translations.literal: On dingmao day Liu Kun was appointed Palace Attendant and Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Liu Kun was named palace attendant and grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 征南軍司戴邈上疏，以為：「喪亂以來，庠序隳廢；

translations.literal: Staff Officer of the Campaigning-South Army Dai Miao submitted a memorial, holding that: "Since the great disorders, schools have been ruined;
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning-South staff officer Dai Miao memorialized: "Since the civil wars, the schools have collapsed;

sentences.zh: 議者或謂平世尚文，遭亂尚武，此言似之，而實不然。

translations.literal: some who discuss the matter say that in peaceful times one values letters and in disorder one values arms — this seems plausible but is not in fact so.
translations.idiomatic: some say that peaceful ages honor learning and troubled ages honor arms. That sounds plausible, but it is wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫儒道深奧，不可倉猝而成。

translations.literal: The Confucian Way is profound and cannot be completed in haste.
translations.idiomatic: The Confucian tradition is deep and cannot be rebuilt overnight.

sentences.zh: 比天下平泰，然後修之，則廢墜已久矣。

translations.literal: If one waits until the empire is at peace and only then restores it, ruin will long since have set in.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until the realm is at peace to restore it, and the decay will have gone too far.

sentences.zh: 又，貴游之子，未必有斬將搴旗之才，從軍征戍之役，不及盛年使之講肄道義，良可惜也。

translations.literal: Moreover, sons of noble houses do not necessarily have the talent to behead generals and seize banners; to put them to campaigning and garrison service without letting them study the Way in their prime years is truly a pity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, sons of the elite are not all born to slay generals and seize banners. To send them to war in their prime without teaching them the Way is a grievous waste.

sentences.zh: 世道久喪，禮俗日弊，猶火之消膏，莫之覺也。

translations.literal: The moral order has long been lost and ritual custom daily declines, like fire consuming fat — yet no one perceives it.
translations.idiomatic: Moral order has been failing for years and ritual decays daily, like fire melting tallow, yet scarcely anyone notices.

sentences.zh: 今王業肇建，萬物權輿，謂宜篤道崇儒，以勵風化。」

translations.literal: Now the royal enterprise is just being founded and all things are in their beginning; I hold that you should devote yourself to the Way, exalt Confucian learning, and thereby encourage transformation by custom."
translations.idiomatic: Your royal enterprise is only now taking shape. This is the moment to honor the Way, elevate Confucian learning, and revive public morals."

sentences.zh: 王從之，始立太學。

translations.literal: The prince followed his advice and for the first time established the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince agreed and founded the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰出畋，以愍帝行車騎將軍，戎服執戟前導。

translations.literal: Han ruler Cong went out hunting and had Emperor Min serve as Acting General of Chariots and Cavalry, in military dress bearing a halberd to lead the way.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong went hunting and made Emperor Min act as his charioteer general, dressed in armor and carrying a halberd to march ahead.

sentences.zh: 見者指之曰：「此故長安天子也。」

translations.literal: Those who saw pointed and said: "That is the former Son of Heaven of Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Onlookers pointed and said: "That is the former emperor of Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 聚而觀之，故老有泣者。

translations.literal: They gathered to watch, and among the old inhabitants some wept.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds gathered to stare, and old men wept.

sentences.zh: 太子粲言於聰曰：「昔周武王豈樂殺紂乎？

translations.literal: Crown Prince Can said to Cong: "In antiquity did King Wu of Zhou take pleasure in killing Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Liu Can told Cong: "Did King Wu of Zhou take pleasure in killing King Zhou?

sentences.zh: 正恐同惡相求，為患故也。

translations.literal: He feared only that those sharing the same evil would seek one another and become a source of harm.
translations.idiomatic: He feared only that evil men would rally to a symbol of the old regime and cause trouble.

sentences.zh: 今興兵聚眾者，皆以子業為名，不如早除之！」

translations.literal: Those who now raise armies and gather crowds all do so in the name of Ziye — better to remove him early!"
translations.idiomatic: Every rebel army marches under Ziye's name. Better kill him now!"

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「吾前殺庾鈱輩，而民心猶如是。

translations.literal: Cong said: "I earlier killed Yu Yin and his party, yet popular sentiment is still like this.
translations.idiomatic: Cong said: "I already killed Yu Yin and his followers, yet the people still feel this way.

sentences.zh: 吾未忍復殺也，且小觀之。」

translations.literal: I cannot bear to kill again; let us observe a little longer."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bring myself to kill again. Let us wait and see."

sentences.zh: 十二月，聰饗群臣於光極殿，使愍帝行酒洗爵，已而更衣，又使之執蓋；

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Cong feasted his ministers in the Hall of Utmost Light, had Emperor Min serve wine and rinse the cups, then after changing clothes had him hold the parasol;
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Cong feasted his ministers in the Hall of Utmost Light, made Emperor Min pour wine and rinse cups, then after changing clothes made him hold the parasol;

sentences.zh: 晉臣多涕泣，有失聲者。

translations.literal: many Jin ministers wept, and some lost control of their voices.
translations.idiomatic: many Jin ministers wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎隴西辛賓起，抱帝大哭，聰命引出，斬之。

translations.literal: Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, Xin Bin of Longxi, rose, embraced the emperor, and wept loudly; Cong ordered him led out and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of Writing gentleman Xin Bin of Longxi rose, embraced the emperor, and wailed. Cong had him taken out and executed.

sentences.zh: 趙固與河內太守郭默侵漢河東，至絳，右司隸部民奔之者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Zhao Gu and Guo Mo, Prefect of Henei, raided Hedong in Han territory as far as Jiang; more than thirty thousand people of the Right Metropolitan Area fled to them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Gu and Henei prefect Guo Mo raided Han Hedong as far as Jiang, and more than thirty thousand people from the right metropolitan region joined them.

sentences.zh: 騎兵將軍劉勳追擊之，殺萬餘人，固、默引歸。

translations.literal: Cavalry General Liu Xun pursued them, killed more than ten thousand, and Gu and Mo withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry general Liu Xun pursued them, killed more than ten thousand, and Gu and Mo withdrew.

sentences.zh: 太子粲帥將軍劉雅生等步騎十萬屯小平津，固揚言曰：「要當生縛劉粲以贖天子。」

translations.literal: Crown Prince Can led Generals Liu Yasheng and others with a hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to encamp at Xiaoping Ford; Gu proclaimed: "I intend to bind Liu Can alive to ransom the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Can camped at Xiaoping Ford with a hundred thousand troops under generals such as Liu Yasheng. Gu declared: "I will take Liu Can alive and trade him for the emperor."

sentences.zh: 粲表於聰曰：「子業若死，民無所望，則不為李矩、趙固之用，不攻而自滅矣。」

translations.literal: Can memorialized Cong: "If Ziye dies, the people will have nothing to hope for, and Li Ju and Zhao Gu will no longer be useful to them; they will perish without our attacking."
translations.idiomatic: Can wrote to Cong: "If Ziye dies, the people lose their rallying point. Li Ju and Zhao Gu will lose their hold on them and collapse without a fight."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，愍帝遇害於平陽。

translations.literal: On wuxu day Emperor Min was murdered at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day Emperor Min was killed at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 粲遣雅生攻洛陽，固奔陽城山。

translations.literal: Can sent Yasheng to attack Luoyang, and Gu fled to Yangcheng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Can sent Yasheng against Luoyang, and Gu fled to Yangcheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 是歲，王命課督農功，二千石、長吏以入谷多少為殿最，諸軍各自佃作，即以為稟。

translations.literal: That year the prince ordered the assessment and supervision of agricultural work; the two-thousand-bushel officials and chief clerks were ranked superior or inferior according to how much grain they delivered, and each army tilled fields for itself and used the yield as rations.
translations.idiomatic: That year the prince ordered agricultural inspections. Prefects and magistrates were ranked by the grain they delivered, and each army farmed for its own rations.

sentences.zh: 氐王楊茂搜卒，長子難敵立，與少子堅頭分領部曲；

translations.literal: Di King Yang Maosou died; his eldest son Nandi succeeded and divided command of the tribes with his younger son Jiantou;
translations.idiomatic: Di king Yang Maosou died. His eldest son Nandi succeeded him and shared command of the tribes with his younger brother Jiantou;

sentences.zh: 難敵號左賢王，屯下辨，堅頭號右賢王，屯河池。

translations.literal: Nandi styled himself Left Worthy King and encamped at Xiabian; Jiantou styled himself Right Worthy King and encamped at Hechi.
translations.idiomatic: Nandi took the title Left Worthy King and camped at Xiabian; Jiantou took the title Right Worthy King and camped at Hechi.

sentences.zh: 河南王吐谷渾卒。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun, King of Henan, died.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun, king of Henan, died.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾者，慕容廆之庶兄也，父涉歸，分戶一千七百以隸之。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun was a son of Murong Hui's father by a concubine; when their father Shegui died, he allotted him seventeen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun was Murong Hui's elder half-brother. When their father Shegui died, he gave Tuyuhun seventeen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 及廆嗣位，二部馬鬥，廆遣使讓吐谷渾曰：「先公分建有別，奈何不相遠異，而令馬有斗傷」吐谷渾怒曰：「馬是六畜，斗乃其常，何至怒及於人！

translations.literal: When Hui succeeded to the position, horses of the two divisions fought; Hui sent an envoy to reproach Tuyuhun, saying: "Our late father divided the domains with clear distinction — why do you not keep far apart and let the horses fight and injure each other?" Tuyuhun angrily said: "Horses are one of the six domestic animals; fighting is their nature — why take anger to the point of blaming men!
translations.idiomatic: When Hui took power, horses from the two divisions fought. Hui sent an envoy to rebuke Tuyuhun: "Our father divided the domains clearly — why do you not keep apart so your horses do not injure one another?" Tuyuhun snapped: "Horses are livestock; they fight by nature. Why take it out on people?

sentences.zh: 欲遠別甚易，恐後會為難耳！

translations.literal: To separate far is very easy — I only fear that meeting again later will be hard!
translations.idiomatic: Keeping apart is easy enough — I only fear we may find it hard to meet again!

sentences.zh: 今當去汝萬里之外。」

translations.literal: I shall now go ten thousand li away from you."
translations.idiomatic: I am going ten thousand li away from you."

sentences.zh: 遂帥其眾西徙。

translations.literal: He then led his people west in migration.
translations.idiomatic: He led his followers west in migration.

sentences.zh: 廆悔之，遣其長史乙那婁馮追謝之。

translations.literal: Hui regretted it and sent his chief clerk Yinalou Feng to pursue him with an apology.
translations.idiomatic: Hui regretted the breach and sent his chief clerk Yinalou Feng after him with an apology.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾曰：「先公嘗稱卜筮之言云：『吾二子皆當強盛，祚流後世。』

translations.literal: Tuyuhun said: "Our late father once cited divination, saying: 'Both my sons will grow mighty and their fortune will flow to later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun said: "Our father once cited a divination: 'Both my sons will grow mighty, and their fortune will endure for generations.

sentences.zh: 我，孽子也，理無並大。

translations.literal: I am a son by a concubine; by right I cannot share greatness with him.
translations.idiomatic: I am a son by a concubine. By right I cannot share power with him.

sentences.zh: 今因馬而別，殆天意乎！」

translations.literal: Now parting because of horses — perhaps this is Heaven's will!"
translations.idiomatic: Now we part over a horse fight — perhaps this is Heaven's design!"

sentences.zh: 遂不復還，西傅陰山而居。

translations.literal: He then never returned, but went west to settle along the Yin Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He never came back, moving west to settle along the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 屬永嘉之亂，因度隴而西，據洮水之西，極於白蘭，地方數千里。

translations.literal: During the Yongjia turmoil, he crossed Long and went west, holding the west of the Tao River, reaching as far as Bailan, with territory of several thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongjia catastrophe struck, he crossed Long Pass westward, seized lands west of the Tao River as far as Bailan, and held a domain of several thousand li.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑謂兄為阿干，廆追思之，為之作《阿干之歌》。

translations.literal: The Xianbei call an elder brother agan; Hui mourned him in memory and composed for him the "Song of Agan."
translations.idiomatic: Among the Xianbei an elder brother is called agan; Murong Hui remembered him fondly and composed the "Song of Agan" in his honor.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾有子六十人，長子吐延嗣。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun had sixty sons; the eldest son Tuyan succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyuhun had sixty sons; his eldest, Tuyan, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 吐延長大有勇力，羌、胡皆畏之。

translations.literal: Tuyan grew tall and had courage and strength; both Qiang and Hu feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyan grew into a man of great stature and valor, feared by Qiang and Hu alike.

sentences.zh: 中宗元皇帝上太興元年（

translations.literal: First year of Taixing, first part of Emperor Yuan of Zhongzong (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Zhongzong (

sentences.zh: 戊寅，公元三一八年）

translations.literal: wuyin, corresponding to 318 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuyin, 318 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，遼西公疾陸眷卒，其子幼，叔父涉復辰自立。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Jilujuan, Duke of Liaoxi, died; his son was young, and his paternal uncle Shefuchen installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, during the first month, Jilujuan, Duke of Liaoxi, died. His heir was still a child, and his uncle Shefuchen seized power for himself.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾自薊往奔喪；

translations.literal: Duan Pidi went from Ji to attend the funeral;
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pidi set out from Ji to attend the funeral;

sentences.zh: 段末柸宣言：「匹磾之來，欲為篡也。」

translations.literal: Duan Mobai declared: "Pidi's coming is intended for usurpation."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Mobai proclaimed: "Pidi is coming to seize power."

sentences.zh: 匹磾至右北平，涉復辰發兵拒之。

translations.literal: When Pidi reached Youbeiping, Shefuchen sent troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Pidi reached Youbeiping, Shefuchen dispatched troops to block him.

sentences.zh: 末柸乘虛襲涉復辰，殺之，並其子弟黨與，自稱單于。

translations.literal: Mobai seized the opportunity to raid Shefuchen, killed him, and together with his sons, younger brothers, and partisans proclaimed himself chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Mobai struck while Shefuchen's forces were engaged, killed him, wiped out his sons, brothers, and followers, and declared himself chanyu.

sentences.zh: 迎擊匹磾，敗之；

translations.literal: He met and attacked Pidi and defeated him;
translations.idiomatic: He turned on Pidi, routed him,

sentences.zh: 匹磾走還薊。

translations.literal: Pidi fled back to Ji.
translations.idiomatic: and Pidi fled back to Ji.

sentences.zh: 三月，癸丑，愍帝凶問至建康，王斬縗居廬；

translations.literal: In the third month, on guichou, news of Emperor Min's death reached Jiankang; the Prince wore hemp and mourned in a hut;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on guichou, word of Emperor Min's death reached Jiankang. The Prince donned mourning garb and withdrew to a mourning hut;

sentences.zh: 百官請上尊號，王不許。

translations.literal: the officials asked him to assume the exalted title, but the Prince would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: the officials pressed him to take the throne, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 紀瞻曰：「晉氏統絕，於今二年，陛下當承大業；

translations.literal: Ji Zhan said: "The house of Jin's line has been severed — it is now two years; Your Majesty ought to inherit the great enterprise;
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhan said: "The imperial line of Jin has been broken for two years now. Your Majesty should take up the great cause;

sentences.zh: 顧望宗室，誰復與讓！

translations.literal: looking about at the imperial clan, who is there to yield to anymore!
translations.idiomatic: Look about the imperial house — to whom could you still yield the throne?

sentences.zh: 若光踐大位，則神、民有所憑依；

translations.literal: if you promptly ascend the throne, then gods and people will have something to rely upon;
translations.idiomatic: If you take the throne at once, gods and people alike will have someone to lean on;

sentences.zh: 苟為逆天時，違人事，大勢一去，不可復還。

translations.literal: if you go against Heaven's season and violate human affairs, once the great momentum is lost it cannot be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: but if you defy Heaven's moment and human expectation, once the tide turns it will never return.

sentences.zh: 今兩都燔蕩，宗廟無主，劉聰竊號於西北，而陛下方高讓於東南，此所謂揖讓而救火也。」

translations.literal: Now both capitals have been burned and swept bare, the ancestral temples have no master, Liu Cong has usurped the title in the northwest, yet Your Majesty is still loftily yielding in the southeast — this is what is called bowing in abdication while fighting a fire."
translations.idiomatic: Both capitals lie in ashes, the ancestral shrines stand masterless, and Liu Cong has seized the imperial title in the northwest — yet Your Majesty still plays at lofty refusal in the southeast. This is like bowing away the throne while the house burns."

sentences.zh: 王猶不許，使殿中將軍韓績徹去御坐。

translations.literal: The Prince still would not agree and sent Palace General Han Ji to remove the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince still refused and ordered Palace General Han Ji to remove the throne.

sentences.zh: 瞻叱績曰：「帝坐上應列星，敢動者斬！」

translations.literal: Zhan shouted at Ji: "The imperial seat corresponds to the stars in their array — whoever dares move it shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhan rebuked Ji: "The imperial seat corresponds to the stars in their courses — touch it and you die!"

sentences.zh: 王為之改容。

translations.literal: The Prince changed expression on account of this.
translations.idiomatic: At that the Prince's manner changed.

sentences.zh: 奉朝請周嵩上疏曰：「古之王者，義全而後取，讓成而後得，是以享世長久，重光萬載也。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Zhou Song submitted a memorial saying: "Ancient kings first completed righteousness and then took power, first perfected yielding and then obtained the throne — hence they enjoyed long reigns and their glory shone for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Gentleman Zhou Song submitted a memorial: "Ancient kings did not take power until righteousness was complete, nor accept the throne until their show of refusal was finished — and so their dynasties endured and their glory shone for ages.

sentences.zh: 今梓宮未返，舊京未清，義夫泣血，士女遑遑。

translations.literal: Now the imperial coffin has not returned, the old capital has not been cleared, men of righteousness weep blood, and gentlemen and ladies are in anxious turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial coffin has not yet returned home, the old capital remains uncleansed, righteous men weep blood, and men and women alike live in dread.

sentences.zh: 宜開延嘉謀，訓卒厲兵，先雪社稷大恥，副四海之心，則神器將安適哉！」

translations.literal: It is fitting to open court for good counsel, drill troops and sharpen weapons, first wash away the great shame of the state altars and match the hearts of all within the four seas — then to whom would the sacred vessel go!"
translations.idiomatic: Hold open court for wise counsel, drill the troops and sharpen arms, first redeem the state's deepest shame and answer the hope of the realm — then who else could rightly receive the Mandate?"

sentences.zh: 由是忤旨，出為新安太守，又坐怨望抵罪。

translations.literal: Because of this he offended the imperial will, was sent out as Administrator of Xin'an, and again was convicted on a charge of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: For this he fell from favor, was posted as Administrator of Xin'an, and was later punished again for discontent.

sentences.zh: 嵩，顗之弟也。

translations.literal: Song was the younger brother of Zhou Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song was the younger brother of Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，王即皇帝位，百官皆陪列。

translations.literal: On bingchen the Prince ascended the imperial throne; all officials stood in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen the Prince took the throne, with the full court in attendance.

sentences.zh: 帝命王導升御床共坐，導固辭曰：「若太陽下同萬物，蒼生何由仰照？」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Wang Dao to ascend the imperial couch and sit together with him; Dao firmly declined, saying: "If the sun came down level with all things, how would the living rely on its light?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor invited Wang Dao to share the imperial couch; Dao firmly refused: "If the sun descended to the level of all things, how could the people beneath look up to its light?"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The Emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor desisted.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元，文武增位二等。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, the era name was changed, and civil and military ranks were raised two grades.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, and raised civil and military ranks by two grades.

sentences.zh: 帝欲賜諸吏投刺勸進者加位一等，民投刺者皆除吏，凡二十餘萬人。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to reward all officials who had submitted memorials urging his accession with one grade promotion, and to appoint as officials all commoners who had submitted such memorials — more than two hundred thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor planned to promote every official who had urged his accession by one rank and appoint every common petitioner as an official — more than two hundred thousand people in all.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍熊遠曰：「陛下應天繼統，率土歸戴，豈獨近者情重，遠者情輕！

translations.literal: Regular Attendant Xiong Yuan said: "Your Majesty has succeeded to the throne in accord with Heaven; all within the realm submits and looks up — how can closeness weigh heavily and distance weigh lightly alone!
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant Xiong Yuan said: "Your Majesty has inherited the throne by Heaven's mandate and the whole realm now looks to you — can nearness alone earn reward while the distant are left out?

sentences.zh: 不若依漢法遍賜天下爵，於恩為普，且可以息檢核之煩，塞巧偽之端也。」

translations.literal: Better to follow Han practice and grant ranks throughout the realm; the favor would be universal, and it could also end the bother of inspection and block the openings for cunning fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Better to follow Han precedent and grant ranks to all under Heaven — the grace would be universal, and it would spare the trouble of verification while closing the door to fraud."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，立王太子紹為皇太子。

translations.literal: On gengwu he established Prince Shao as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he named Crown Prince Shao heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子仁孝，喜文辭，善武藝，好賢禮士，容受規諫，與庾亮、溫嶠等為布衣之交。

translations.literal: The crown prince was benevolent and filial, fond of literary composition, skilled in martial arts, delighted in honoring the worthy and treating scholars with courtesy, open to admonition, and counted Yu Liang, Wen Jiao, and others among his friends from common days.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was humane and filial, fond of letters, skilled in arms, eager to honor the worthy and treat scholars with respect, receptive to remonstrance, and close friends with Yu Liang, Wen Jiao, and others from before he wore the crown.

sentences.zh: 亮風格峻整，善談老、莊，帝器重之，聘亮妹為太子妃。

translations.literal: Liang's bearing was stern and orderly; he was skilled in discoursing on Laozi and Zhuangzi; the Emperor greatly valued him and betrothed Liang's younger sister as the crown prince's consort.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's manner was austere and precise, and he was adept at discourse on Laozi and Zhuangzi. The Emperor thought highly of him and betrothed Liang's sister to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 帝以賀循行太子太傅，周顗為少傅，庾亮以中書郎侍講東宮。

translations.literal: The Emperor made He Xun Grand Tutor of the crown prince, Zhou Yi Junior Tutor, and Yu Liang, as Palace Secretary, lectured in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed He Xun Grand Tutor to the heir, Zhou Yi Junior Tutor, and made Yu Liang, as Palace Secretary, lecture in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝好刑名家，以《韓非》書賜太子。

translations.literal: The Emperor favored the Legalist school and bestowed the book of Han Fei on the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor favored Legalist thought and gave the crown prince the Han Feizi.

sentences.zh: 庾亮諫曰：「申、韓刻薄傷化，不足留聖心。」

translations.literal: Yu Liang remonstrated, saying: "Shen Buhai and Han Fei are harsh and injure transformation — they are not fit to occupy the sage mind."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Liang remonstrated: "The doctrines of Shen Buhai and Han Fei are harsh and corrosive — they should not occupy a sage ruler's mind."

sentences.zh: 太子納之。

translations.literal: The crown prince accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince took his advice.

sentences.zh: 帝復遣使授慕容廆龍驤將軍、大單于、昌黎公，廆辭公爵不受。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent envoys to confer on Murong Hui the titles of General Who Exerts Might, Grand Chanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui declined the ducal title and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor again sent envoys to appoint Murong Hui General Who Exerts Might, Grand Chanyu, and Duke of Changli; Hui refused the ducal title.

sentences.zh: 廆以游邃為龍驤長史，劉翔為主簿，命邃創定府朝儀法。

translations.literal: Hui made You Sui Longxiang Chief Clerk and Liu Xiang Registrar, and ordered Sui to establish ritual and law for the headquarters court.
translations.idiomatic: Hui appointed You Sui Chief Clerk of the Longxiang command and Liu Xiang Registrar, charging Sui with drafting court ritual for his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 裴嶷言於廆曰：「晉室衰微，介居江表，威德不能及遠，中原之亂，非明公不能拯也。

translations.literal: Pei Ni said to Hui: "The house of Jin is in decline, holding only the land south of the river; its prestige and virtue cannot reach far — the turmoil of the central plains, none but Your Excellency can rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ni told Hui: "The Jin court has waned, clinging to lands south of the Yangtze; its authority no longer reaches far. None but you can rescue the central plains from chaos.

sentences.zh: 今諸部雖各擁兵，然皆頑愚相聚，宜以漸並取，以為西討之資。」

translations.literal: Now though the various divisions each hold troops, they are but stupid masses gathered together — you should gradually annex them and use them as resources for a western campaign."
translations.idiomatic: The various tribes may each hold armies, but they are crude bands clustered together. You should absorb them step by step and use them as the foundation for a campaign westward."

sentences.zh: 廆曰：「君言大，非孤所及也。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Your words are grand — they are beyond what I alone can reach.
translations.idiomatic: Hui replied: "Your vision is vast — beyond what I can achieve alone.

sentences.zh: 然君中朝名德，不以孤僻陋而教誨之，是天以君賜孤而祐其國也。」

translations.literal: Yet you are a man of renowned virtue from the central court; that you do not disdain this remote and humble place to instruct me means Heaven has given you to me to bless my state."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you are a man of fame and virtue from the central court, and you do not disdain this remote corner to guide me — Heaven has sent you to bless my realm."

sentences.zh: 乃以嶷為長史，委以軍國之謀；

translations.literal: He then made Ni Chief Clerk and entrusted him with military and state planning;
translations.idiomatic: He then made Ni Chief Clerk and entrusted him with strategy for army and state;

sentences.zh: 諸部弱小者，稍稍擊取之。

translations.literal: the weaker divisions he gradually attacked and seized.
translations.idiomatic: and he gradually attacked and absorbed the weaker tribes.

sentences.zh: 李矩使郭默、郭誦救趙固，屯於洛汭。

translations.literal: Li Ju sent Guo Mo and Guo Song to rescue Zhao Gu, and they encamped at the Luorui ford.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju sent Guo Mo and Guo Song to relieve Zhao Gu, and they encamped at the Luorui ford.

sentences.zh: 誦潛遣其將耿稚等夜濟河襲漢營，漢貝丘王翼光覘知之，以告太子粲，請為之備。
