translations.literal: Song secretly sent his generals Geng Zhi and others to cross the river by night and raid the Han camp; Yiguang, Prince of Beiqiu of Han, detected it by scouting and reported to Crown Prince Can, asking that preparations be made.
translations.idiomatic: Song secretly sent Generals Geng Zhi and others to cross the river by night and strike the Han camp. Yiguang, Prince of Beiqiu, discovered the move through scouts and warned Crown Prince Can to prepare.

sentences.zh: 粲曰：「彼聞趙固之敗，自保不暇，安敢來此邪！

translations.literal: Can said: "Having heard of Zhao Gu's defeat, they can scarcely protect themselves — how would they dare come here!
translations.idiomatic: Can said: "They've heard Zhao Gu was beaten — they can barely save themselves. How would they dare come here?

sentences.zh: 毋為驚動將士！」

translations.literal: Do not alarm the officers and soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: Don't alarm the troops!"

sentences.zh: 俄而稚等奄至，十道進攻，粲眾驚潰，死傷太半，粲走保陽鄉。

translations.literal: Soon Geng Zhi and the others suddenly arrived, advancing in ten columns; Can's force panicked and fled; more than half were killed or wounded, and Can fled to defend Yangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later Geng Zhi's force was upon them, attacking in ten columns. Can's army broke in panic; more than half were killed or wounded, and Can fled to Yangxiang.

sentences.zh: 稚等據其營，獲器械、軍資不可勝數。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others seized their camp and captured weapons and military supplies beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhi's men seized the camp and captured weapons and supplies beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 及旦，粲見稚等兵少，更與劉雅生收餘眾攻之，漢主聰使太尉范隆帥騎助之，與稚等相持，苦戰二十餘日，不能下。

translations.literal: At dawn Can saw that Zhi and the others had few troops; he gathered the remnant force with Liu Yasheng and attacked again; Han ruler Cong sent Grand Commandant Fan Long at the head of cavalry to assist; they stalemate with Zhi and the others, fighting bitterly for more than twenty days without bringing them down.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Can saw how few Geng Zhi's men were and rallied the survivors with Liu Yasheng to counterattack. Emperor Cong sent Grand Commandant Fan Long with cavalry to help. The battle dragged on for more than twenty brutal days without either side breaking the other.

sentences.zh: 李矩進兵救之，漢兵臨河拒守，矩兵不得濟。

translations.literal: Li Ju advanced troops to rescue them; Han forces guarded the riverbank and blocked them, and Ju's troops could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju marched to their relief, but Han troops held the riverbank and kept his forces from crossing.

sentences.zh: 稚等殺其所獲牛馬，焚其軍資，突圍，奔虎牢。

translations.literal: Zhi and the others slaughtered the cattle and horses they had captured, burned their military supplies, broke out of encirclement, and fled to Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Zhi's men slaughtered their captured livestock, burned the supplies they had taken, broke out, and fled to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 詔以矩都督河南三郡諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ju Grand Commander over the military affairs of the three commanderies of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Li Ju commander over military affairs in the three Henan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 漢螽斯則百堂災，燒殺漢主聰之子會稽王康等二十一人。

translations.literal: At the Han palace, the Baixue Hall in the Locust District suffered fire disaster, burning to death Emperor Cong's son Kang, Prince of Kuaiji, and twenty others.
translations.idiomatic: Fire broke out in the Baixue Hall of the Locust Quarter in the Han palace, killing Emperor Cong's son Kang, Prince of Kuaiji, and twenty others.

sentences.zh: 聰以其子濟南王驥為大將軍、都督中外諸軍事、錄尚書，齊王勱為大司徒。

translations.literal: Cong made his son Ji, Prince of Jinan, Grand General, Commander over all military affairs within and without, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Qi Yue he made Grand Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Cong appointed his son Ji, Prince of Jinan, Grand General, supreme commander of all armies, and chief overseer of the Masters of Writing; he made Prince of Qi Yue Grand Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 焦嵩、陳安舉兵逼上邽，相國保遣使告急於張寔，寔遣金城太守竇濤督步騎二萬赴之。

translations.literal: Jiao Song and Chen An raised troops and pressed Shanggui; Chancellor Bao sent messengers in urgent appeal to Zhang Shi; Shi sent Jincheng Administrator Dou Tao at the head of twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Song and Chen An raised armies and besieged Shanggui. Chancellor Bao sent desperate appeals to Zhang Shi, who dispatched Jincheng Administrator Dou Tao with twenty thousand foot and horse soldiers.

sentences.zh: 軍至新陽，聞愍帝崩，保謀稱尊號。

translations.literal: When the army reached Xinyang, they heard that Emperor Min had died; Bao planned to assume the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Xinyang, word came that Emperor Min was dead; Bao planned to proclaim himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 破羌都尉張誥言於寔曰：「南陽王，國之疏屬，忘其大恥而亟欲自尊，必不能成功。

translations.literal: Poyang Commandant Zhang Gao said to Shi: "The Prince of Nanyang is a distant branch of the imperial house; forgetting the great shame he is eager to exalt himself — he is sure not to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang Commandant Zhang Gao told Shi: "The Prince of Nanyang is a distant imperial kinsman who, forgetting the realm's deepest shame, is rushing to exalt himself — he cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 晉王近親，且有名德，當帥天下以奉之。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin is a close kinsman and moreover has fame and virtue — he should lead the realm in serving him."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin is a close kinsman of proven virtue — you should lead the realm in acknowledging him."

sentences.zh: 寔從之，遣牙門蔡忠奉表詣建康；

translations.literal: Shi followed this advice and sent Gate Officer Cai Zhong with a memorial to Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: Shi agreed and sent Gate Officer Cai Zhong to Jiankang with a loyal memorial;

sentences.zh: 比至，帝已即位。

translations.literal: by the time he arrived, the Emperor had already ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: but by the time he arrived the new emperor was already enthroned.

sentences.zh: 寔不用江東年號，猶稱建興。

translations.literal: Shi did not use the era name of Jiangdong but still called the era Jianxing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi kept the era name Jianxing and did not adopt the new reign title used in the lower Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁丑朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on dingchou, the first day of the month, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the first day of the fourth month, dingchou, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 加王敦江州牧，王導驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Wang Dun was additionally made Governor of Jiangzhou; Wang Dao was made Cavalry General-in-Chief with authority equal to the Three Excellencies and permission to maintain a headquarters staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun was additionally appointed Governor of Jiangzhou; Wang Dao was made Cavalry General-in-Chief with a grand minister's staff and privileges equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 導遣八部從事行揚州郡國，還，同時俱見。

translations.literal: Dao sent the eight department aides to inspect the commanderies and kingdoms of Yangzhou; when they returned, he received them all at once.
translations.idiomatic: Dao dispatched his eight department aides to inspect Yangzhou's commanderies and kingdoms; when they returned he received them all together.

sentences.zh: 諸從事各言二千石官長得失，獨顧和無言。

translations.literal: Each aide spoke of the gains and faults of the two-thousand-bushel officials; only Gu He remained silent.
translations.idiomatic: Each aide reported on the successes and failures of local administrators; only Gu He said nothing.

sentences.zh: 導問之，和曰：「明公作輔，寧使網漏吞舟，何緣采聽風聞，以察察為政邪！」

translations.literal: Dao asked him; He said: "Your Excellency serves as chief minister — would you rather let the net miss great fish than gather hearsay and govern with minute scrutiny!"
translations.idiomatic: When Dao pressed him, He replied: "As chief minister, would you not rather let the net miss the big fish than govern by picking up rumors and nitpicking every detail?"

sentences.zh: 導咨嗟稱善。

translations.literal: Dao sighed in admiration and praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Dao sighed and praised him.

sentences.zh: 和，榮之族子也。

translations.literal: He was a clansman of Gu Rong's branch.
translations.idiomatic: Gu He was a kinsman of Gu Rong.

sentences.zh: 成丞相范長生卒；

translations.literal: Fan Changsheng, Chancellor of Cheng, died;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Changsheng, chancellor of Cheng, died;

sentences.zh: 成主雄以長生子侍中賁為丞相。

translations.literal: Lord of Cheng Xiong made Changsheng's son Ben, a Palace Attendant, Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Xiong of Cheng appointed Changsheng's son Ben, a palace attendant, as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 長生博學，多藝能，年近百歲，蜀人奉之如神。

translations.literal: Changsheng was broadly learned and had many talents; nearing a hundred years of age, the people of Shu revered him as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Changsheng was deeply learned and master of many arts; nearing a hundred, the people of Shu revered him almost as a deity.

sentences.zh: 漢中常侍王沈養女有美色，漢主聰立以為左皇后。

translations.literal: Wang Shen, a Han palace attendant, had a foster daughter of beautiful appearance; Han ruler Cong installed her as Left Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Wang Shen had a foster daughter renowned for her beauty; Emperor Cong made her Left Empress.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王鑒、中書監崔懿之、中書令曹恂諫曰：「臣聞王者立後，比德乾坤，生承宗廟，沒配后土。

translations.literal: Minister of Writing Wang Jian, Palace Secretary Supervisor Cui Yizhi, and Palace Secretary Cao Xun remonstrated, saying: "We have heard that when a king establishes an empress, she is matched to Heaven and Earth in virtue; in life she inherits the ancestral temples, in death she is paired with Hou Tu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Minister of Writing; Cui Yizhi, Palace Secretary Supervisor; and Cao Xun, Palace Secretary, remonstrated: "When a king chooses an empress, she should mirror Heaven and Earth in virtue — sustaining the ancestral temples in life and joining Hou Tu in death.

sentences.zh: 必擇世德名宗，幽閒令淑，乃副四海之望，稱神祇之心。

translations.literal: One must choose a family of hereditary virtue and eminent lineage, serene and modest, virtuous and gentle — only then does she answer the hopes of all within the four seas and accord with the hearts of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: She must come from a house of hereditary virtue and eminent lineage, modest and gracious — only then can she satisfy the realm and win the spirits' approval.

sentences.zh: 孝成帝以趙飛燕為後，使繼嗣絕滅，社稷為墟，此前鑒也。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng of Han made Zhao Feiyan empress, causing the succession to be cut off and the state altars to become ruins — this is a prior warning.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng made Zhao Feiyan empress, and the line died out and the altars crumbled — that lesson stands before us.

sentences.zh: 自麟嘉以來，中宮之位，不以德舉。

translations.literal: Since Linjia, the position in the inner palace has not been filled by virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Linjia era the inner palace has not been filled on grounds of virtue.

sentences.zh: 借使沈之弟女，刑餘小丑，猶不可以塵污椒房，況其家婢邪！

translations.literal: Even if it were Shen's younger brother's daughter — a mutilated court eunuch's brat — she still could not stain the pepper chambers with dust; how much less a servant girl from his household!
translations.idiomatic: Even Shen's own niece — a eunuch's wretched offspring — would still defile the empress's chambers; how much less a servant girl from his house!

sentences.zh: 六宮妃嬪，皆公子公孫，奈何一旦以婢主之！

translations.literal: The consorts of the six palaces are all sons and grandsons of dukes — how can a servant girl suddenly be made to rule them!
translations.idiomatic: The consorts of the six palaces are all noble-born — how can a maid be set over them in a day!

sentences.zh: 臣恐非國家之福也。」

translations.literal: We fear this is not a blessing for the state."
translations.idiomatic: We fear this bodes ill for the state."

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，使中常侍宣懷謂太子粲曰：「鑒等小子，狂言侮慢，無復君臣上下之禮，其速考實！」

translations.literal: Cong flew into a rage and sent Palace Attendant Xuan Huai to tell Crown Prince Can: "Jian and those whelp fellows — their wild words are insulting and contemptuous; there is no longer observance of the rites between ruler and minister, high and low — investigate and verify them at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Cong was furious and sent Palace Attendant Xuan Huai to tell Crown Prince Can: "Jian and his crew have spewed arrogant insults and cast off all propriety between ruler and subject — investigate them at once!"

sentences.zh: 於是收鑒等送市，皆斬之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jian and the others were seized and sent to the market; all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and the others were arrested, marched to the market, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 金紫光祿大夫王延馳將入諫，門者弗通。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, galloped to enter and remonstrate, but the gatekeepers would not admit him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan, Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, rode at speed to remonstrate, but the gatekeepers refused him entry.

sentences.zh: 鑒等臨刑，王沈以杖叩之曰：「庸奴，復能為惡乎！

translations.literal: As Jian and the others faced execution, Wang Shen struck them with a staff, saying: "Useless slaves — can you still do evil!
translations.idiomatic: At the execution Wang Shen beat them with a staff: "Worthless curs — can you still make trouble now!

sentences.zh: 乃公何與汝事！」

translations.literal: What business of yours was it with this old man!"
translations.idiomatic: What was any of this to do with you!"

sentences.zh: 鑒瞋目叱之曰：「豎子，滅大漢者，正坐汝鼠輩與靳准耳！

translations.literal: Jian glared and shouted at him: "You whelp — those who will destroy Great Han are precisely you rat pack and Jin Zhun!
translations.idiomatic: Jian glared at him and shouted: "You brat — it is vermin like you and Jin Zhun who will destroy Great Han!

sentences.zh: 要當訴汝於先帝，取汝於地下治之。」

translations.literal: I shall surely bring my case against you before the Former Emperor and take you below ground to settle accounts."
translations.idiomatic: I will accuse you before the late emperor and drag you under the earth to answer for this."

sentences.zh: 准謂鑒曰：「吾受詔收君，有何不善，君言漢滅由吾也！」

translations.literal: Jin Zhun said to Jian: "I received the edict to take you — what wrong is there in that? You say Great Han's destruction is because of me!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun said to Jian: "I act on imperial orders — what crime is that? You blame me for Han's ruin!"

sentences.zh: 鑒曰：「汝殺皇太弟，使主上獲不友之名。

translations.literal: Jian said: "You killed the Grand Imperial Younger Brother and made our lord obtain the name of being unfilial among brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered: "You murdered the Grand Imperial Younger Brother and left our lord with the name of an unfilial brother.

sentences.zh: 國家畜養汝輩，何得不滅！」

translations.literal: The state has raised and fed you lot — how could it not be destroyed!"
translations.idiomatic: The state has nurtured creatures like you — how can it fail to perish!"

sentences.zh: 懿之謂准曰：「汝心如梟獍，必為國患，汝既食人，人亦當食汝。」

translations.literal: Cui Yizhi said to Jin Zhun: "Your heart is like an owl or jackal devouring its parent — you will surely be a calamity to the state. Since you have eaten men, men shall also eat you."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yizhi told Jin Zhun: "Your heart is that of a beast that devours its own kind — you are bound to bring disaster on the realm. You have fed on others; others will feed on you in turn."

sentences.zh: 聰又立宣懷養女為中皇后。

translations.literal: Cong then installed Xuan Huai's foster daughter as Central Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Cong went on to make Xuan Huai's adopted daughter his Central Empress.

sentences.zh: 司徒荀組在許昌，逼於石勒，帥其屬數百人渡江。

translations.literal: Minister over the Masses Xun Zu was at Xuchang; pressed by Shi Le, he led several hundred of his followers across the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Minister over the Masses Xun Zu was trapped at Xuchang by Shi Le and led several hundred followers across the Yangzi to the south.

sentences.zh: 詔組與太保西陽王羕並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Zu and Grand Guardian Prince Xi Yang (Yang) jointly to handle matters in the Ministry of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Xun Zu and Grand Guardian Prince Xi Yang (Yang) to share responsibility for the Ministry of Writing.

sentences.zh: 段匹磾之奔疾陸眷喪也，劉琨使其世子群送之。

translations.literal: When Duan Pidi went in haste to attend Lu Juan's funeral, Liu Kun sent his heir apparent Liu Qun to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Pidi hurried off to mourn Lu Juan, Liu Kun dispatched his heir Liu Qun to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 匹磾敗，群為段末柸所得。

translations.literal: Pidi was defeated, and Liu Qun was captured by Duan Mocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi suffered defeat, and Liu Qun fell into the hands of Duan Mocheng.

sentences.zh: 末柸厚禮之，許以琨為幽州刺史，欲與之襲匹磾，密遣使繼群書，請琨為內應，為匹磾邏騎所得。

translations.literal: Mocheng treated him with great courtesy, promising to make Liu Kun Governor of You Province, and planned with him to strike Pidi; he secretly sent a messenger carrying Qun's letter, asking Kun to serve as an inside collaborator, but it was seized by Pidi's patrol scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Mocheng received him with every honor and promised to appoint Liu Kun Governor of Youzhou, intending to join forces against Pidi. He secretly sent a messenger with a letter from Qun urging Kun to act as an inside collaborator, but Pidi's scouts intercepted it.

sentences.zh: 時琨別屯征北小城，不知也，來見匹磾。

translations.literal: At the time Liu Kun was separately encamped at the northern expedition's small fort and knew nothing of this; he came to see Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun was camped separately at a small fort on the northern front and knew nothing of the plot. He came to visit Pidi.

sentences.zh: 匹磾以群書示琨曰：「意亦不疑公，是以白公耳。」

translations.literal: Pidi showed Liu Kun Qun's letter and said: "In my heart I do not suspect you, sir — that is why I have informed you."
translations.idiomatic: Pidi showed Liu Kun the letter and said: "I never doubted you — that is why I am telling you openly."

sentences.zh: 琨曰：「與公同盟，庶雪國家之恥，若兒書密達，亦終不以一子之故負公而忘義也。」

translations.literal: Liu Kun said: "I am allied with you, sir, hoping to wipe away the state's shame. Even if my son's letter had reached you in secret, I would never for one child's sake betray you and forget righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun replied: "We are allies in the cause of restoring the realm. Even if my son's letter had reached you secretly, I would never betray our bond for the sake of one child."

sentences.zh: 匹磾雅重琨，初無害琨意，將聽還屯。

translations.literal: Pidi had always held Liu Kun in high esteem and at first had no intent to harm him; he was about to allow him to return to his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi had long respected Liu Kun and never intended to harm him; he was about to let him return to his camp.

sentences.zh: 其弟叔軍謂匹磾曰：「我，胡夷耳；

translations.literal: His younger brother Shujun said to Pidi: "We are Hu barbarians —
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shujun said to Pidi: "We are Hu barbarians —

sentences.zh: 所以能服晉人者，畏吾眾也。

translations.literal: the reason we can make the Jin people submit is that they fear our numbers.
translations.idiomatic: the only reason the Jin people submit to us is fear of our strength.

sentences.zh: 今我骨肉乖離，是其良圖之日；

translations.literal: Now our own flesh and blood are estranged — this is the day for them to carry out their fine scheme;
translations.idiomatic: Now that our own kin are turning against us, this is their chance to strike;

sentences.zh: 若有奉琨以起，吾族盡矣。」

translations.literal: if someone raises Liu Kun to revolt, our entire clan will be wiped out."
translations.idiomatic: if they rally behind Liu Kun, our whole clan is finished."

sentences.zh: 匹磾攻拔之。

translations.literal: Pidi attacked and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Pidi attacked and seized the fort.

sentences.zh: 代郡太守辟閭嵩、後將軍韓據復潛謀襲匹磾，事洩，匹磾執嵩、據及其徒黨，悉誅之。

translations.literal: Dai Commandery Prefect Pilu Song and Rear General Han Ju again secretly plotted to strike Pidi; when the affair leaked out, Pidi seized Song, Ju, and their followers and executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Pilu Song, prefect of Dai Commandery, and Rear General Han Ju again plotted secretly against Pidi. When the conspiracy was exposed, Pidi arrested Song, Ju, and their followers and put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 五月，癸丑，匹磾稱詔收琨，縊殺之，並殺其子侄四人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on day guichou, Pidi claimed an imperial edict to arrest Liu Kun, strangled him to death, and also killed four of his sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the guichou day, Pidi claimed authority to arrest Liu Kun by imperial order, had him strangled, and killed four of his sons and nephews as well.

sentences.zh: 琨從事中郎盧諶、崔悅等帥琨餘眾奔遼西，依段末柸，奉劉群為主；

translations.literal: Liu Kun's Attendant Gentleman Lu Chen, Cui Yue, and others led Kun's remaining troops to flee to Liaoxi, relying on Duan Mocheng and making Liu Qun their leader;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen and Cui Yue, Liu Kun's aides, led his remaining forces into Liaoxi, took refuge with Duan Mocheng, and rallied around Liu Qun as their leader;

sentences.zh: 將佐多奔石勒。

translations.literal: many of his officers and aides fled to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Many of his officers and staff defected to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 悅，林之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Yue was the great-grandson of Cui Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yue was a great-grandson of Cui Lin.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以匹磾尚強，冀其能平河朔，乃不為琨舉哀。

translations.literal: The court, because Pidi was still strong and hoping he could pacify Heshuo, therefore did not hold mourning rites for Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: The court, still counting on the powerful Pidi to pacify the north, declined to mourn Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 溫嶠表：「琨盡忠帝室，家破身亡，宜在褒恤。」

translations.literal: Wen Qiao submitted a memorial: "Liu Kun gave his full loyalty to the imperial house; his family was destroyed and he lost his life — he deserves commendation and consolation."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao memorialized the throne: "Liu Kun gave everything for the imperial house — his family ruined, his life forfeited. He deserves honor and relief."

sentences.zh: 盧諶、崔悅因末柸使者，亦上表為琨訟冤。

translations.literal: Through Mocheng's envoy, Lu Chen and Cui Yue also submitted memorials pleading Liu Kun's case.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chen and Cui Yue sent memorials through Duan Mocheng's envoy as well, petitioning on Liu Kun's behalf.

sentences.zh: 後數歲，乃贈琨太尉、侍中，謚曰愍。

translations.literal: Several years later, Liu Kun was posthumously granted Grand Commandant and Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Min.
translations.idiomatic: Only years later was Liu Kun posthumously named Grand Commandant and Palace Attendant, with the posthumous title Min ("Lamented").

sentences.zh: 於是夷、晉以琨死故，皆不附匹磾。

translations.literal: Thereupon both the tribesmen and the Jin people, because of Liu Kun's death, all refused to submit to Pidi.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Kun's death, both tribal peoples and Jin loyalists turned away from Pidi.

sentences.zh: 末柸遣其弟攻匹磾，匹磾帥其眾數千將奔邵續，勒將石越邀之於鹽山，大敗之，匹磾復還保薊。

translations.literal: Mocheng sent his younger brother to attack Pidi; Pidi led several thousand of his followers intending to flee to Shao Xu, but Shi Le's general Shi Yue intercepted him at Yanshan and inflicted a great defeat; Pidi again returned to hold Jicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Mocheng sent his brother against Pidi. Pidi gathered several thousand men and tried to flee to Shao Xu, but Shi Le's general Shi Yue intercepted him at Mount Yan and routed his force. Pidi retreated once more to Jicheng.

sentences.zh: 末柸自稱幽州刺史。

translations.literal: Mocheng styled himself Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Mocheng proclaimed himself Governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，溫嶠為劉琨奉表詣建康，其母崔氏固止之，嶠絕裾而去。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wen Qiao was carrying Liu Kun's memorial to Jiankang, his mother Lady Cui firmly tried to stop him; Qiao tore his robe's hem free and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wen Qiao set out for Jiankang bearing Liu Kun's memorial, his mother Lady Cui tried hard to stop him. He tore free of her grasp — ripping the hem of his robe — and left.

sentences.zh: 既至，屢求返命，朝廷不許，會琨死，除散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: After he arrived, he repeatedly asked to return and report, but the court did not permit it; when Liu Kun died, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, he repeatedly asked permission to return north, but the court refused. When Liu Kun died, he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Dispersed Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 嶠聞母亡，阻亂不得奔喪、臨葬，固讓不拜，苦請北歸。

translations.literal: Wen Qiao heard that his mother had died; blocked by disorder, he could not rush to mourn or attend the burial; he firmly declined the appointment and bitterly pleaded to return north.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Qiao learned his mother had died, the chaos of war prevented him from going home to mourn or attend her burial. He refused the appointment and pleaded desperately to return north.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「凡行禮者，當使理可經通。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In all matters of conducting rites, principle must be able to run through and connect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's reply read: "Rites must be grounded in what reason can sustain.

sentences.zh: 今桀逆未梟，諸軍奉迎梓宮猶未得進，嶠以一身，於何濟其私難而不從王命邪！」

translations.literal: Now the rebel has not yet been executed, and the armies escorting the imperial coffin still cannot advance — with Wen Qiao's single person, how can private grief be served by disobeying the royal command!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebel has not yet been destroyed, and the armies escorting the imperial coffin still cannot move. How can one man's private grief outweigh obedience to the throne?"

sentences.zh: 嶠不得已受拜。

translations.literal: Wen Qiao had no choice but to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Qiao had no choice but to accept.

sentences.zh: 初，曹嶷既據青州，乃叛漢來降。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Cao Yi had seized Qing Province, he rebelled against Han and came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Cao Yi had taken control of Qingzhou, he broke with the Han state and surrendered to Jin.

sentences.zh: 又以建康懸遠，勢援不接，復與石勒相結，勒授嶷東州大將軍、青州牧，封琅邪公。

translations.literal: Then, because Jiankang was far away and no support could reach him, he again allied with Shi Le; Le granted Yi the title of Grand General of the Eastern Province and Governor of Qing Province, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Jiankang too distant for effective support, he allied himself with Shi Le again. Le made him Grand General of the Eastern Provinces and Governor of Qingzhou, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Langya.

sentences.zh: 六月，甲申，以刁協為尚書令，荀崧為左僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day jiashen, Diao Xie was appointed Minister of Writing and Xun Song Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the jiashen day, Diao Xie was named Minister of Writing and Xun Song Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 協性剛悍，與物多忤，與侍中劉隗懼為帝所寵任；

translations.literal: Diao Xie was by nature fierce and unyielding, at odds with many people; he and Palace Attendant Liu Kai were both favored and entrusted by the emperor;
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie was fierce and uncompromising, often at odds with others. He and Palace Attendant Liu Kai were both deeply favored by the emperor;

sentences.zh: 欲矯時弊，每崇上抑下，排沮豪強，故為王氏所疾，諸刻碎之政，皆雲隗、協所建。

translations.literal: wishing to rectify the abuses of the age, they always exalted superiors and restrained inferiors, blocking and suppressing the powerful great clans; therefore they were resented by the Wang clan, and all the niggling, petty policies were said to be creations of Liu Kai and Diao Xie.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to reform the abuses of the day, they consistently favored the throne over the great families and moved against powerful clans. The Wang faction despised them, and every harsh, finicky policy was blamed on Liu Kai and Diao Xie.

sentences.zh: 協又使酒放肆，侵毀公卿，見者皆側目憚之。

translations.literal: Diao Xie also abused wine and acted recklessly, insulting and slandering the high ministers; all who saw him glanced sideways in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Xie also drank heavily and behaved outrageously, insulting the highest ministers. Everyone who saw him flinched.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，封皇子晞為武陵王。

translations.literal: On day wuxu, Prince Xi was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, Prince Xi was enfeoffed as Prince of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 劉虎自朔方侵拓跋鬱律西部。

translations.literal: Liu Hu from Shuofang invaded the western territory of Tuoba Yulü.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu of Shuofang raided the western domains of Tuoba Yulü.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，鬱律擊虎，大破之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Yulü struck Liu Hu and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, Yulü attacked Liu Hu and routed him.

sentences.zh: 虎走出塞，從弟路孤帥其部落降於鬱律。

translations.literal: Liu Hu fled beyond the frontier; his younger cousin's son Lugu led his tribe to surrender to Yulü.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu fled beyond the border. His clansman Lugu led their tribe in surrender to Yulü.

sentences.zh: 於是鬱律西取烏孫故地，東兼勿吉以西，士馬精強，雄於北方。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yulü took the former lands of the Wusun in the west and in the east annexed the region west of the Wuji; with elite troops and horses he was paramount in the north.
translations.idiomatic: Yulü then seized the old Wusun territories in the west and extended eastward to include the lands west of the Wuji. With crack troops and horses, he became the dominant power of the north.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰寢疾，征大司馬曜為丞相，石勒為大將軍，皆隸尚書事，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: Han ruler Liu Cong fell gravely ill; he summoned Grand Marshal Liu Yao as Chancellor and Shi Le as Grand General, both subordinate to the Ministry of Writing, to receive the deathbed edict and assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong fell gravely ill. He summoned Grand Marshal Liu Yao as Chancellor and Shi Le as Grand General, both to serve under the Ministry of Writing and receive his deathbed charge to govern jointly.

sentences.zh: 曜、勒固辭。

translations.literal: Liu Yao and Shi Le firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao and Shi Le both firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 乃以曜為丞相、領雍州牧，勒為大將軍、領幽、冀二州牧，勒辭不受。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Yao was made Chancellor and concurrently Governor of Yong Province, and Shi Le Grand General and concurrently Governor of You and Ji Provinces; Le declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Cong then named Liu Yao Chancellor and Governor of Yongzhou, and Shi Le Grand General with authority over Youzhou and Jizhou — but Le refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 以上洛王景為太宰，濟南王驥為大司馬，昌國公顗為太師，朱紀為太傅，呼延晏為太保，並錄尚書事；

translations.literal: Prince Shangluo (Jing) was made Grand Mentor, Prince Jinan (Ji) Grand Marshal, Duke of Changguo (Yi) Grand Preceptor, Zhu Ji Grand Tutor, and Huyan Yan Grand Guardian — all to handle matters in the Ministry of Writing;
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Prince Shangluo (Jing) Grand Mentor, Prince Jinan (Ji) Grand Marshal, Duke of Changguo (Yi) Grand Preceptor, Zhu Ji Grand Tutor, and Huyan Yan Grand Guardian — all to share responsibility for the Ministry of Writing;

sentences.zh: 范隆守尚書令、儀同三司，靳准為大司空、領司隸校尉，皆迭決尚書奏事。

translations.literal: Fan Long retained Minister of Writing and Three Excellencies Equivalent in Honor; Jin Zhun was made Grand Minister of Works and concurrently Imperial Inspector of the Capital District — all deciding memorials to the Ministry of Writing in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Long remained Minister of Writing with honors equal to the Three Excellencies. Jin Zhun became Grand Minister of Works and Inspector of the Capital District. They took turns deciding affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，聰卒。

translations.literal: On day guihai, Liu Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day, Liu Cong died.

sentences.zh: 甲子，太子粲即位。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, Crown Prince Can ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, Crown Prince Can took the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后靳氏為皇太后，樊氏號弘道皇后，武氏號弘德皇后，王氏號弘孝皇后；

translations.literal: Empress Jin was honored as Empress Dowager; Lady Fan was styled Empress of Grand Way, Lady Wu Empress of Grand Virtue, and Lady Wang Empress of Grand Filial Piety;
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jin was elevated to Empress Dowager. Lady Fan was styled Grand Way Empress, Lady Wu Grand Virtue Empress, and Lady Wang Grand Filial Empress;

sentences.zh: 立其妻靳氏為皇后，子元公為太子。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Jin was installed as empress, and his son Prince Yuan as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He installed his wife Lady Jin as empress and named his son Prince Yuan crown prince.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元漢昌。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed and the era name was changed to Hanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Hanchang.

sentences.zh: 葬聰於宣光陵，謚曰昭武皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Liu Cong was buried at Xuanguang Mausoleum; his posthumous title was Emperor Zhaowu and his temple name Liezong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was buried at Xuanguang Mausoleum with the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu and temple name Liezong.

sentences.zh: 靳太后等皆年未盈二十，粲多行無禮，無復哀戚。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Jin and the others were all not yet twenty years of age; Can frequently behaved without propriety and showed no further grief.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Jin and the other consorts were all under twenty. Can disported himself without restraint and showed no sign of mourning.

sentences.zh: 靳准陰有異志，私謂粲曰：「如聞諸公欲行伊、霍之事，先誅太保及臣，以大司馬統萬機，陛下宜早圖之！」

translations.literal: Jin Zhun secretly harbored divergent ambitions and privately said to Can: "I hear that the high ministers wish to play the parts of Yi and Huo — first execute the Grand Guardian and me, then let the Grand Marshal control all affairs of state; Your Majesty should act early!"
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun nursed secret ambitions. Privately he told Can: "I hear the senior ministers mean to play Yi Yin and Huo Guang — kill the Grand Guardian and me first, then put the Grand Marshal in charge of everything. Your Majesty should strike before they do!"

sentences.zh: 粲不從。

translations.literal: Can did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Can refused.

sentences.zh: 准懼，復使二靳氏言之，粲乃從之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun grew afraid and again had the two Ladies Jin speak to him; Can then complied.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Jin Zhun had the two Empresses Jin press the case. Can finally agreed.

sentences.zh: 收其太宰景、大司馬驥、驥母弟車騎大將軍吳王逞、太師顗、大司徒齊王勱，皆殺之。

translations.literal: He seized Grand Mentor Jing, Grand Marshal Ji, Ji's younger maternal brother General of Chariots and Cavalry Prince Wu (Cheng), Grand Preceptor Yi, and Grand Minister of Education Prince Qi (Mo) — all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Can arrested Grand Mentor Jing, Grand Marshal Ji, Ji's younger maternal brother Prince Wu (Cheng), Grand Preceptor Yi, and Grand Minister of Education Prince Qi (Mo) — and had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 朱紀、范隆奔長安。

translations.literal: Zhu Ji and Fan Long fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji and Fan Long fled to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 八月，粲治兵於上林，謀討石勒。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Can marshaled troops at Shanglin and planned to campaign against Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Can mustered troops at Shanglin, planning an expedition against Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 以丞相曜為相國、都督中外諸軍事，仍鎮長安；

translations.literal: Chancellor Liu Yao was made Chancellor of State and Director of All Military Affairs Inside and Outside, still garrisoning Chang'an;
translations.idiomatic: He made Chancellor Liu Yao Chancellor of State and supreme commander of all forces, keeping him at Chang'an;

sentences.zh: 靳准為大將軍、錄尚書事。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun was made Grand General and put in charge of the Ministry of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: and Jin Zhun Grand General with control of the Ministry of Writing.

sentences.zh: 粲常游宴後宮。

translations.literal: Can frequently feasted and revelled in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Can spent his days feasting in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 軍國之事，一決於准。

translations.literal: Matters of army and state were all decided by Jin Zhun alone.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter of war and state was Jin Zhun's alone to decide.

sentences.zh: 准矯詔以從弟明為車騎將軍，康為衛將軍。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun forged an edict appointing his younger clansman Jin Ming General of Chariots and Cavalry and Jin Kang Defender General.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun forged an edict making his clansmen Jin Ming General of Chariots and Cavalry and Jin Kang Defender General.

sentences.zh: 准將作亂，謀於王延。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun was about to rebel and consulted Wang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun was preparing a coup and confided in Wang Yan.

sentences.zh: 延弗從，馳，將告之；

translations.literal: Wang Yan refused; he galloped off, intending to report it;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan refused and galloped off to expose the plot;

sentences.zh: 遇靳康，劫延以歸。

translations.literal: he encountered Jin Kang, who seized Yan and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: but Jin Kang intercepted him and dragged him back.

sentences.zh: 准遂勒兵升光極殿，使甲士執粲，數而殺之，謚曰隱帝。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun then led troops up to the Hall of Grand Ultimate, had armored soldiers seize Can, listed his crimes and killed him; his posthumous title was Emperor Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun then marched his troops into the Hall of Grand Ultimate, had Can seized by armored guards, denounced his crimes, and killed him — posthumous title: Emperor Yin.

sentences.zh: 劉氏男女，無少長皆斬東市。

translations.literal: Men and women of the Liu clan, young and old without distinction, were all beheaded at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: Every man and woman of the Liu clan, young and old alike, was executed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 發永光、宣光二陵，斬聰屍，焚其宗廟。

translations.literal: The Yongguang and Xuanguang mausoleums were opened; Liu Cong's corpse was beheaded and the ancestral temples burned.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the Yongguang and Xuanguang tombs, beheaded Liu Cong's corpse, and burned the ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 准自號大將軍、漢天王，稱制，置百官，謂安定胡嵩曰：「自古無胡人為天子者，今以傳國璽付汝，還如晉家。」

translations.literal: Jin Zhun styled himself Grand General and Heavenly King of Han, assumed regency, established the full bureaucracy, and said to Hu Song of Anding: "From antiquity no Hu man has been Son of Heaven; now I give you the Imperial Seal of Transmission — return it to the house of Jin."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun proclaimed himself Grand General and Heavenly King of Han, assumed imperial authority, and installed a full bureaucracy. To Hu Song of Anding he said: "No barbarian has ever truly ruled as Son of Heaven. Take the Imperial Seal and restore it to the Jin."

sentences.zh: 嵩不敢受；

translations.literal: Hu Song dared not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song dared not accept.

sentences.zh: 准怒，殺之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun in anger killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun killed him in a rage.

sentences.zh: 遣使告司州刺史李矩曰：「劉淵，屠各小丑，因晉之亂。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to tell Governor of Si Province Li Ju: "Liu Yuan was a petty Tuge bandit who exploited Jin's disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Li Ju, Governor of Sizhou: "Liu Yuan was a petty Tuge chieftain who seized on Jin's collapse.

sentences.zh: 矯稱天命，使二帝幽沒。

translations.literal: He falsely claimed the Mandate of Heaven and caused the Two Emperors to perish in obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely claimed Heaven's mandate and brought the Two Emperors to a shameful end.

sentences.zh: 輒帥眾扶侍梓宮，請以上聞。」

translations.literal: I have now led the masses to escort the imperial coffin and request that this be reported above."
translations.idiomatic: I have now gathered forces to escort the imperial coffin north and ask that you report this to the throne."

sentences.zh: 矩馳表於帝，帝遣太常韓胤等奉迎梓宮。

translations.literal: Li Ju galloped a memorial to the emperor; the emperor sent Grand Master of Ceremonies Han Yin and others to escort the imperial coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju rushed word to the emperor, who dispatched Grand Master of Ceremonies Han Yin and others to receive the coffin.

sentences.zh: 漢尚書北宮純等招集晉人，堡於東宮，靳康攻滅之。

translations.literal: Han Minister of Writing Beigong Chun and others gathered Jin people and fortified themselves in the Eastern Palace; Jin Kang attacked and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: Beigong Chun and other Han ministers rallied Jin loyalists in a fort at the Eastern Palace. Jin Kang attacked and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 准欲以王延為左光祿大夫，延罵曰：「屠各逆奴，何不速殺我！

translations.literal: Jin Zhun wished to make Wang Yan Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness; Yan cursed, saying: "Tuge rebel slave — why don't you kill me quickly!
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun offered Wang Yan the post of Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness. Wang Yan raged: "Tuge rebel — kill me now if you dare!

sentences.zh: 以吾左目置西陽門，觀相國之入也；

translations.literal: Place my left eye at the Xiyang Gate to watch the Chancellor of State enter;
translations.idiomatic: Plant my left eye at the Xiyang Gate to watch Liu Yao march in;

sentences.zh: 右目置建春門，觀大將軍之入也！」

translations.literal: my right eye at the Jianchun Gate to watch the Grand General enter!"
translations.idiomatic: and my right eye at the Jianchun Gate to watch Shi Le ride in!"

sentences.zh: 准殺之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun had him killed.

sentences.zh: 相國曜聞亂，自長安赴之。

translations.literal: Chancellor of State Liu Yao heard of the disorder and came from Chang'an to deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of State Liu Yao heard of the coup and rushed from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 石勒帥精銳五萬以討准，據襄陵北原。

translations.literal: Shi Le led fifty thousand picked troops to campaign against Jin Zhun and encamped on the northern plain of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marched fifty thousand elite troops against Jin Zhun and camped on the plain north of Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 准數挑戰，勒堅壁以挫之。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun repeatedly challenged to battle; Shi Le held his walls firm to wear him down.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun repeatedly offered battle; Shi Le held his lines and refused to engage.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，曜至赤壁。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, Liu Yao reached Chibi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, Liu Yao reached Chibi.

sentences.zh: 太保呼延晏等自平陽歸之，與太傅朱紀等共上尊號。

translations.literal: Grand Guardian Huyan Yan and others returned to him from Pingyang; together with Grand Tutor Zhu Ji and others they offered him the supreme title.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Huyan Yan and others came from Pingyang to join him. Together with Grand Tutor Zhu Ji and the rest, they urged Liu Yao to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 曜即皇帝位，大赦，惟靳准一門不在赦例。

translations.literal: Liu Yao immediately ascended the imperial throne; a general amnesty was proclaimed, except that the entire clan of Jin Zhun was excluded from the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao took the throne at once and proclaimed a general amnesty — except for the house of Jin Zhun, which was excluded entirely.

sentences.zh: 改元光初。

translations.literal: The era name was changed to Guangchu.
translations.idiomatic: The era name was changed to Guangchu.

sentences.zh: 以朱紀領司徒，呼延晏領司空，太尉范隆以下悉復本位。

translations.literal: Zhu Ji was put in charge of the Ministry of Education, Huyan Yan in charge of the Ministry of Works; Grand Commandant Fan Long and all below were restored to their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ji became Minister of Education, Huyan Yan Minister of Works, and Grand Commandant Fan Long and the rest were restored to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 以石勒為大司馬、大將軍，加九錫，增封十郡，進爵為趙公。

translations.literal: Shi Le was made Grand Marshal and Grand General, granted the Nine Bestowals, given ten additional commanderies in enfeoffment, and advanced in rank to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le was named Grand Marshal and Grand General, granted the Nine Bestowals, given ten additional commanderies, and ennobled as Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 勒進攻准於平陽，巴及羌、羯降者十餘萬落，勒皆徙之於所部郡縣。

translations.literal: Shi Le pressed the attack on Jin Zhun at Pingyang; more than a hundred thousand families of Ba people and Qiang, Jie, and others who had surrendered were all relocated by Le to the commanderies and counties under his control.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le pressed the siege of Jin Zhun at Pingyang. More than a hundred thousand surrendered Ba, Qiang, and Jie households were resettled across the territories under his command.

sentences.zh: 漢主曜使征北將軍劉雅、鎮北將軍劉策屯汾陰，與勒共討准。

translations.literal: Han ruler Liu Yao sent Northern Campaign General Liu Ya and Northern Garrison General Liu Ce to encamp at Fenyin, joining Shi Le in campaigning against Jin Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Han emperor Liu Yao dispatched Northern Campaign General Liu Ya and Northern Garrison General Liu Ce to camp at Fenyin and join Shi Le against Jin Zhun.

sentences.zh: 十一月，乙卯，日夜出，高三丈。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on day yimao, there was a day-night star, three zhang in height.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the yimao day, a daybreak star appeared, towering three zhang high.

sentences.zh: 詔以王敦為荊州牧，加陶侃都督交州諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Wang Dun Governor of Jingzhou and additionally made Tao Kan Commander-in-Chief over the military affairs of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Wang Dun governor of Jingzhou and made Tao Kan commander over military affairs in Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 敦固辭州牧，乃聽為刺史。

translations.literal: Dun firmly declined the governorship, whereupon he was permitted to serve as Inspector instead.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun firmly declined the governorship and was allowed to remain inspector instead.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔群公卿士各陳得失。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, an edict ordered all dukes, ministers, and officials each to set forth what was right and what was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day, an edict called on all the great officers and officials to speak frankly of the court's strengths and failings.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞熊遠上疏，以為：「胡賊猾夏，梓宮未返，而不能遣軍進討，一失也；

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xiong Yuan submitted a memorial, stating: "The barbarian invaders are cunning in the Central Realm, the imperial coffin has not yet returned, yet no army is sent forward to campaign against them — this is the first failure;
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xiong Yuan submitted a memorial arguing: "Barbarian raiders run riot in the heartland, the imperial coffin still has not come home, and yet no army is sent to strike them — that is the first failure;

sentences.zh: 群官不以仇賊未報為恥，務在調戲、酒食而已，二失也；

translations.literal: the assembled officials do not take it as shame that the enemy has not been avenged, but devote themselves only to banter and feasting — this is the second failure;
translations.idiomatic: the officials feel no shame that the enemy remains unavenged and busy themselves only with jest and feasting — that is the second failure;

sentences.zh: 選官用人，不料實德，惟在白望，不求才幹，惟事請托，當官者以治事為俗吏，奉法為苛刻，盡禮為諂諛，從容為高妙，放蕩為達士，驕蹇為簡雅，三失也；

translations.literal: in selecting and appointing men, real virtue is not weighed, only empty reputation is sought; talent and capacity are not sought, only patronage is served; those in office take handling affairs for vulgar clerks, obeying law for harsh severity, observing every courtesy for flattery, ease for lofty refinement, dissipation for enlightened gentlemen, and arrogance and obstinacy for simple elegance — this is the third failure;
translations.idiomatic: in appointments, real merit counts for nothing while empty reputation decides all; patronage replaces talent; officeholders treat diligence as clerkish, lawfulness as harshness, courtesy as flattery, ease as refinement, dissipation as enlightenment, and arrogance as elegance — that is the third failure;

sentences.zh: 世之所惡者，陸沈泥滓；

translations.literal: what the age hates is sinking into the mire;
translations.idiomatic: what the age despises is sinking into the mud;

sentences.zh: 時之所善者，翱翔雲霄。

translations.literal: what the times praise is soaring in the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: what the times applaud is soaring above the clouds.

sentences.zh: 是以萬機未整，風俗偽薄。

translations.literal: Therefore the myriad affairs of state are not put in order, and custom is false and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, state affairs remain unsettled and public morals hollow and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 朝廷群司，以從順為善，相違見貶，安得朝有辨爭之臣，士無祿仕之志乎！

translations.literal: The assembled offices of the court take compliance as good and see contradiction punished — how can the court have ministers who dispute and debate, or gentlemen who lack the will to seek office for salary!
translations.idiomatic: Every office at court treats compliance as virtue and punishes dissent — how can there be ministers willing to argue in open debate, or gentlemen who still seek office for the public good rather than a salary!

sentences.zh: 古之取士，敷奏以言；

translations.literal: In antiquity, in selecting scholars, presentation and speech were used;
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, men were chosen by how they spoke and presented themselves;

sentences.zh: 今光祿不試，甚違古義。

translations.literal: now the Director of Retainers does not test them — this greatly violates the ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: today the Director of Retainers no longer examines candidates at all — a grave departure from ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 又舉賢不出世族，用法不及權貴，是以才不濟務，奸無所懲。

translations.literal: Moreover, recommended worthies do not come from outside the great clans, and the law does not reach the powerful and noble; therefore talent does not meet the tasks, and the wicked have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men are drawn only from the great clans, and the law never touches the powerful — so talent fails the state's needs and the wicked go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 若此道不改，求以救亂，難矣！」

translations.literal: If this way is not changed, to seek salvation from disorder will be hard!"
translations.idiomatic: Unless this course is changed, there is little hope of saving the realm from chaos!"

sentences.zh: 先是，帝以離亂之際，欲慰悅人心，州郡秀、孝至者，不試，普皆署吏。

translations.literal: Earlier, because it was a time of separation and disorder, the emperor wished to soothe and please men's hearts; when Filial and Incorrupt candidates arrived from the provinces and commanderies, they were not tested and were all appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the turmoil of civil war, the emperor had sought to reassure the people: Filial and Incorrupt candidates arriving from the provinces were exempted from examination and appointed to office outright.

sentences.zh: 尚書陳頵亦上言：「宜漸循舊制，試以經策。」

translations.literal: Minister of Writing Chen Yun also submitted a statement: "It is fitting gradually to follow the old system and test them on the classics and policy questions."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Writing Chen Yun also urged: "The court should gradually restore the old system and examine candidates on the classics and policy essays."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，仍詔：「不中科者，刺史、太守免官。」

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and further issued an edict: "Those who fail the examination shall cause their Inspector and Prefect to be removed from office."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and added an edict: "If a candidate fails the examination, the inspector and prefect who recommended him shall be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 於是秀、孝皆不敢行，其有到者，亦皆托疾，比三年無就試者。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Filial and Incorrupt candidates all dared not travel; those who did arrive all pleaded illness, and for nearly three years none presented themselves for examination.
translations.idiomatic: At that, recommended candidates refused to travel at all; those who had already arrived pleaded illness, and for nearly three years not one came forward to be examined.

sentences.zh: 帝欲特除孝廉已到者官，尚書郎孔坦奏議，以為：「近郡懼累君父，皆不敢行；

translations.literal: The emperor wished specially to appoint those Filial and Incorrupt candidates who had already arrived, but Secretariat Gentleman Kong Tan submitted a memorial arguing: "The nearby commanderies, fearing to bring trouble on their lords and fathers, all dared not travel;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to appoint the Filial and Incorrupt candidates who had already arrived, but Secretariat Gentleman Kong Tan argued: "Candidates from nearby commanderies, fearing to ruin their recommending officials, refused to travel;

sentences.zh: 遠郡冀於不試，冒昧來赴。

translations.literal: the distant commanderies hoped there would be no examination and came rashly to attend.
translations.idiomatic: those from distant commanderies, hoping to escape examination, came anyway in reckless hope of reward.

sentences.zh: 今若偏加除署，是為謹身奉法者失分，僥倖投射者得官，頹風傷教，恐從此始。

translations.literal: If now special appointments are granted only to some, this would mean that those who kept themselves careful and obeyed the law would lose their due, while lucky opportunists would gain office — a corrupting wind that wounds instruction, and I fear it would begin here.
translations.idiomatic: If the court now appoints only those who arrived, the careful and law-abiding will be cheated while lucky opportunists gain office — a corrupt precedent that could ruin public morals for good.

sentences.zh: 不若一切罷歸，而為之延期，使得就學，則法均而令信矣。」

translations.literal: Better to dismiss them all and return them home, yet extend the deadline so they may pursue study — then the law would be even and the command trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Better to send them all home, extend the deadline, and let them prepare properly — then the law would be fair and the command respected."

sentences.zh: 帝從之，聽孝廉申至七年乃試。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this and permitted Filial and Incorrupt candidates to petition for extension until the seventh year before being examined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this and allowed Filial and Incorrupt candidates to petition for deferral until the seventh year before examination.

sentences.zh: 坦，愉之從子也。

translations.literal: Tan was the son of Kong Yu's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Tan was a nephew of Kong Yu.

sentences.zh: 靳准使侍中卜泰送乘輿、服御，請和於石勒，勒囚泰，送於漢主曜。

translations.literal: Jin Zhun sent Palace Attendant Bu Tai to deliver the imperial carriage and regalia and sue for peace with Shi Le; Le imprisoned Tai and sent him to Han ruler Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhun sent Palace Attendant Bu Tai with the imperial carriage and regalia to sue for peace with Shi Le. Le imprisoned Tai and sent him to Han ruler Liu Yao.

sentences.zh: 曜謂泰曰：「先帝末年，實亂大倫。

translations.literal: Yao said to Tai: "In the late years of the Former Emperor, the great human relations were truly thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Yao told Tai: "In his final years the Former Emperor truly overturned the natural order of the realm.

sentences.zh: 司空行伊、霍之權，使朕及此，其功大矣。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works exercised the authority of Yi and Huo, enabling me to reach this position — his merit is great.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works wielded the power of Yi Yin and Huo Guang and put me on the throne — his service was immense.

sentences.zh: 若早迎大駕者，當悉以政事相委，況免死乎！

translations.literal: If he had earlier welcomed the imperial carriage, I would have entrusted him with all affairs of government — to say nothing of sparing his life!
translations.idiomatic: Had he welcomed the imperial carriage sooner, I would have entrusted him with the whole government — to say nothing of sparing his life!

sentences.zh: 卿為朕入城，具宣此意。」

translations.literal: You, for me, enter the city and fully proclaim this intent."
translations.idiomatic: Go back into the city for me and make this intention fully known."

sentences.zh: 泰還平陽，准自以殺曜母兄，沈吟未從。

translations.literal: Tai returned to Pingyang; Zhun, considering that he had killed Yao's mother and elder brother, hesitated and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Tai returned to Pingyang, but Zhun — knowing he had killed Yao's mother and elder brother — wavered and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 十二月，左、右車騎將軍喬泰、王騰、衛將軍靳康等相與殺准，推尚書令靳明為主，遣卜泰奉傳國六璽降漢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Left and Right Generals of Chariots and Cavalry Qiao Tai and Wang Teng, Defender General Jin Kang, and others jointly killed Zhun, set up Minister of Writing Jin Ming as leader, and sent Bu Tai bearing the six imperial seals of transmission to surrender to Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Left and Right Generals of Chariots and Cavalry Qiao Tai and Wang Teng, Defender General Jin Kang, and others killed Zhun together, made Minister of Writing Jin Ming their leader, and sent Bu Tai with the six imperial seals to surrender to Han.

sentences.zh: 石勒大怒，進軍攻明；

translations.literal: Shi Le was greatly enraged and advanced his army to attack Ming;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le was furious and marched against Jin Ming;

sentences.zh: 明出戰，大敗，乃嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Ming went out to battle, suffered a great defeat, and then tied himself to the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Ming gave battle, was routed, and then shut himself inside the city to hold out.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，封皇子煥為琅邪王。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, the emperor's son Huan was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day, the emperor enfeoffed his son Huan as Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 煥，鄭夫人之子，生二年矣，帝愛之，以其疾篤，故王之。

translations.literal: Huan was the son of Lady Zheng; he had lived two years. The emperor loved him and, because his illness was grave, therefore made him a prince.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was Lady Zheng's son, only two years old. The emperor adored him and, because the boy was gravely ill, enfeoffed him as a prince.

sentences.zh: 己卯，薨。

translations.literal: On day jimao, he died.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day, he died.

sentences.zh: 帝以成人之禮葬之，備吉凶儀服，營起園陵，功費甚廣。

translations.literal: The emperor buried him with the rites of adulthood, provided full auspicious and inauspicious ceremonial garments, and raised a park tomb — the labor and expense were very great.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor buried him with full adult rites, complete ceremonial dress for life and death, and built a princely tomb and park at enormous expense.

sentences.zh: 琅邪國右常侍會稽孫霄上疏諫曰：「古者凶荒殺禮，況今海內喪亂，憲章舊制，猶宜節省。

translations.literal: Right Regular Attendant of the Langya State, Sun Xiao of Kuaiji, submitted a remonstrance saying: "In antiquity, in years of famine and disaster rites were reduced — how much more now, when the realm within the seas is in mourning and disorder, should the old statutes and regulations still be observed with restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xiao of Kuaiji, Right Regular Attendant of Langya, remonstrated: "In ancient times, rites were cut back in famine and disaster — how much more now, with the empire in chaos, should old regulations be kept with restraint!

sentences.zh: 而禮典所無，顧崇飾如是乎！

translations.literal: Yet what the ritual canon does not provide — why honor and adorn it to this degree!
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the ritual canon never prescribed — why honor it with such lavish display!

sentences.zh: 竭已罷之民，營無益之事，殫已困之財，修無用之費，此臣之所不安也。」

translations.literal: To exhaust a people already worn out, undertaking useless affairs; to spend out already strained wealth, undertaking useless expenses — this is what unsettles your subject."
translations.idiomatic: To drain a people already exhausted for useless work, and spend a treasury already empty on useless expense — that is what troubles your servant."

sentences.zh: 帝不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 彭城內史周撫殺沛國內史周默，以其眾降石勒。

translations.literal: Pengcheng Interior Secretary Zhou Fu killed Pei Interior Secretary Zhou Mo and, with his force, surrendered to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng interior secretary Zhou Fu killed Pei interior secretary Zhou Mo and surrendered to Shi Le with his troops.

sentences.zh: 詔下邳內史劉遐領鼓城內史，與徐州刺史蔡豹、泰山太守徐龕共討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Xiapi Interior Secretary Liu Xia acting Interior Secretary of Gucheng, joining Xuzhou Inspector Cai Bao and Taishan Prefect Xu Kan in campaigning against him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict put Xiapi interior secretary Liu Xia in charge as Pengcheng interior secretary and ordered him, with Xuzhou inspector Cai Bao and Taishan prefect Xu Kan, to suppress Zhou Fu.

sentences.zh: 豹，質之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Bao was the great-great-grandson of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Bao was the great-great-grandson of Cai Zhi.

sentences.zh: 石虎帥幽、冀之兵會石勒攻平陽，靳明屢敗，遣使求救於漢。

translations.literal: Shi Hu led the troops of You and Ji to join Shi Le in attacking Pingyang; Jin Ming was repeatedly defeated and sent envoys to Han begging for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu led troops from Youzhou and Jizhou to join Shi Le in the assault on Pingyang. Jin Ming suffered repeated defeats and sent envoys begging Han for help.

sentences.zh: 漢主曜使劉雅、劉策迎之，明帥平陽士女萬五千人奔漢。

translations.literal: Han ruler Liu Yao sent Liu Ya and Liu Ce to welcome him; Ming led fifteen thousand men and women of Pingyang in flight to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Yao sent Liu Ya and Liu Ce to receive him. Jin Ming fled to Han with fifteen thousand men and women from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 曜西屯粟邑，收靳氏男女，無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Yao encamped west at Suyi, seized the men and women of the Jin clan, and beheaded them all without regard to age.
translations.idiomatic: Yao encamped west at Suyi, seized every man and woman of the Jin clan, and beheaded them without regard to age.

sentences.zh: 曜迎其母胡氏之喪於平陽，葬於粟邑，號曰陽陵，謚曰宣明皇太后。

translations.literal: Yao welcomed the coffin of his mother, Lady Hu, from Pingyang and buried her at Suyi; the tomb was called Yangling, and she was given the posthumous title Empress Dowager Xuanming.
translations.idiomatic: Yao brought his mother Lady Hu's coffin from Pingyang and buried her at Suyi in a tomb called Yangling, posthumously titled Empress Dowager Xuanming.

sentences.zh: 石勒焚平陽宮室，使裴憲、石會修永光、宣光二陵，收漢主粲已下百餘口葬之，置戍而歸。

translations.literal: Shi Le burned the palace buildings of Pingyang, had Pei Xian and Shi Hui repair the Yongguang and Xuangguang tombs, gathered more than a hundred persons from Han ruler Can downward and buried them, set garrisons, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le burned the palaces of Pingyang, put Pei Xian and Shi Hui to restoring the Yongguang and Xuangguang tombs, gathered more than a hundred members of Han ruler Can's house for burial, left garrisons, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 成梁州刺史李鳳數有功，成主雄兄子稚在晉壽，疾之。

translations.literal: Li Feng, Governor of Liangzhou under Cheng, had repeatedly achieved merit; Zhi, the son of Lord of Cheng Xiong's elder brother, was at Jinshou and resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Feng, Cheng's governor of Liangzhou, had won repeated victories, but Zhi — a nephew of Lord of Cheng Xiong — was at Jinshou and hated him.

sentences.zh: 鳳以巴西叛，雄自至涪，使太傅驤討鳳，斬之；

translations.literal: Feng rebelled with Baxi; Xiong came in person to Fu, sent Grand Tutor Xiang to campaign against Feng, and beheaded him;
translations.idiomatic: When Feng rebelled from Baxi, Xiong went in person to Fu, sent Grand Tutor Li Xiang against him, and had him executed;

sentences.zh: 以李壽為前將軍，督巴西軍事。

translations.literal: he made Li Shou Forward General and Supervisor of the military affairs of Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Li Shou Forward General with command over military affairs in Baxi.
